Volume 304 Biographies 192: Officials 1 - Zheng He, Jin Ying, Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, Huai En, Wang Zhi, Liang Fang, He Ding, Li Guang, Jiang Cong, Liu Jin, Zhang Yong, Gu Dayong

1
明太祖既定江左，鑒前代之失，置宦者不及百人。 迨末年頒《祖訓》，乃定為十有二監及各司局，稍稱備員矣。 然定制，不得兼外臣文武銜，不得御外臣冠服，官無過四品，月米一石，衣食於內庭。 嘗鐫鐵牌置宮門曰：「內臣不得干預政事，預者斬。 」敕諸司不得與文移往來。 有老閹供事久，一日從容語及政事，帝大怒，即日斥還鄉。 嘗用杜安道為御用監。 安道，外臣也，以鑷工侍帝數十年，帷幄計議皆與知，性縝密不泄，過諸大臣前一揖不啟口而退。 太祖愛之，然亡他寵異，後遷出為光祿寺卿。 有趙成者，洪武八年以內侍使河州市馬。 其後以市馬出者，又有司禮監慶童等，然皆不敢有所干竊。 建文帝嗣位，御內臣益嚴，詔出外稍不法，許有司械聞。 及燕師逼江北，內臣多逃入其軍，漏朝廷虛實。 文皇以為忠於己，而狗兒輩復以軍功得幸，即位後遂多所委任。 永樂元年，內官監李興奉敕往勞暹羅國王。 三年，遣太監鄭和帥舟師下西洋。 八年，都督譚青營有內官王安等。 又命馬靖鎮甘肅，馬騏鎮交阯。 十八年置東廠，令刺事。 蓋明世宦官出使、專征、監軍、分鎮、刺臣民隱事諸大權，皆自永樂間始。
Eunuchs. After the Ming founder had secured the lower Yangzi, he took warning from the failings of earlier dynasties and kept fewer than a hundred eunuchs. By the end of his reign, when he issued the Ancestral Injunctions, they were fixed at twelve directorates and various offices, and could only just be said to be fully staffed. But the established regulations forbade them from holding civilian or military titles outside the inner court, from wearing the hats and robes of outer ministers, and limited their rank to no higher than the fourth; they received one dan of rice a month and were housed and fed in the inner palace. He once had an iron plaque engraved and placed at the palace gate, saying: Inner servants must not interfere in government affairs; anyone who does so shall be executed. He also ordered the various offices not to exchange written documents with them. There was an old eunuch who had long served the court; one day he spoke casually about government affairs, and the emperor was furious and expelled him back to his hometown that same day. He once employed Du Andao as Director of Imperial Services. Andao was a commoner who served the emperor for several decades as a maker of tweezers; he was privy to all the plans and deliberations in the tented camp, was by nature meticulous and secretive, and whenever he passed the great ministers he would bow once and leave without saying a word. The Ming founder favored him, but did not grant him any other special favor; later he was transferred out as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. There was one Zhao Cheng; in the eighth year of Hongwu he was sent as an inner attendant to buy horses in Hezhou. Later there were also those sent out to buy horses, such as Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, but none of them dared to meddle or pilfer anything. When the Jianwen Emperor succeeded to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants even more severely; he issued an edict that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, the local authorities were permitted to arrest and report them. When the Yan army pressed against the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants fled into its ranks and leaked the court's weaknesses. The Yongle Emperor considered them loyal to him, and Gou'er and the others were further favored because of military merit; once he came to the throne, he entrusted them with many responsibilities. In the first year of Yongle, the inner-court official Li Xing was ordered to go and present condolences to the king of Siam. In the third year, Zheng He was sent with a fleet as envoy to the Western Ocean. In the eighth year, at General Tan Qing's camp there were inner officials such as Wang An. He also ordered Ma Jing to garrison Gansu and Ma Qi to garrison Jiaozhi. In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was established and ordered to investigate matters. The great powers exercised by eunuchs in foreign missions, independent campaigns, military supervision, regional garrisons, and spying on the hidden affairs of ministers and commoners all began in the Yongle years.
2
初，太祖制，內臣不許讀書識字。 後宣宗設內書堂，選小內侍，令大學士陳山教習之，遂為定制。 用是多通文墨，曉古今，逞其智巧，逢君作奸。 數傳之後，勢成積重，始於王振，卒於魏忠賢。 考其禍敗，其去漢、唐何遠哉。 雖間有賢者，如懷恩、李芳、陳矩輩，然利一而害百也。 今摭其有關成敗者，作《宦官傳》。
At first, the Ming founder decreed that inner servants were not allowed to read books or learn characters. Later the Xuande Emperor established an inner school hall, selected young inner attendants, and ordered the Grand Secretary Chen Shan to teach them, thus making it a fixed institution. As a result many became literate, understood past and present affairs, and used their intelligence and craftiness to curry favor and commit wrongdoing. After several generations, the abuse had become entrenched, beginning with Wang Zhen and ending with Wei Zhongxian. Looking at the disasters they caused, how far were they from those of the Han and Tang? Though there were occasional worthy men, such as Huai'en, Li Fang, and Chen Ju, the harm they caused outweighed the benefit of one. So now I have collected the cases relevant to success and failure and composed the Biography of Eunuchs.
3
鄭和，雲南人，世所謂三保太監者也。 初事燕王於藩邸，從起兵有功。 累擢太監。 成祖疑惠帝亡海外，欲蹤跡之，且欲耀兵異域，示中國富強。 永樂三年六月，命和及其儕王景弘等通使西洋。 將士卒二萬七千八百餘人，多賫金幣。 造大舶，修四十四丈、廣十八丈者六十二。 自蘇州劉家河泛海至福建，復自福建五虎門揚帆，首達占城，以次遍歷諸番國，宣天子詔，因給賜其君長，不服則以武懾之。 五年九月，和等還，諸國使者隨和朝見。 和獻所俘舊港酋長。 帝大悅，爵賞有差。 舊港者，故三佛齊國也，其酋陳祖義，剽掠商旅。 和使使招諭，祖義詐降，而潛謀邀劫。 和大敗其眾，擒祖義，獻俘，戮於都市。
Zheng He. Zheng He was a man of Yunnan, the one known in the world as the Three-Bao eunuch. At first he served the Prince of Yan in the princely residence and won merit by following him in his uprising. He was repeatedly promoted to eunuch. Chengzu suspected that Emperor Hui had died overseas, wanted to trace him, and also wished to display arms in foreign lands and show China's wealth and strength. In the sixth month of the third year of Yongle, he ordered Zheng He and his fellows Wang Jinghong and others to serve as envoys to the Western Ocean. They had more than twenty-seven thousand eight hundred soldiers and carried large quantities of gold and valuables. They built giant ships, sixty-two of them forty-four zhang long and eighteen zhang wide. They sailed from Liujiagang in Suzhou to Fujian, then again set sail from Wuhumen in Fujian; first they reached Champa, and then in turn visited all the foreign states, proclaiming the emperor's edict, granting gifts to their rulers, and using military force to overawe those who would not submit. In the ninth month of the fifth year, He and the others returned, and envoys from the various states accompanied him to court. He presented the captive chieftain of Jiu'gang. The emperor was greatly pleased and graded the rewards and honors accordingly. Jiu'gang was the former kingdom of Srivijaya; its chieftain, Chen Zuyi, plundered merchant ships. He sent envoys to summon him and pacify him; Zuyi feigned surrender while secretly plotting an ambush and robbery. He utterly defeated his forces, captured Zuyi, presented the prisoners, and had him executed in the marketplace.
4
六年九月，再往錫蘭山。 國王亞烈苦柰兒誘和至國中，索金幣，發兵劫和舟。 和覘賊大眾既出，國內虛，率所統二千餘人，出不意攻破其城，生擒亞烈苦柰兒及其妻子官屬。 劫和舟者聞之，還自救，官軍復大破之。 九年六月獻俘於朝。 帝赦不誅，釋歸國。 是時，交阯已破滅，郡縣其地，諸邦益震詟，來者日多。
In the ninth month of the sixth year they went again to Ceylon. King Alakeshvara lured He into the country, demanded gold and valuables, and sent troops to seize He's ships. He saw that the enemy's main force had gone out and the country was empty, so he led the more than two thousand men under his command and, catching them off guard, attacked and took the city, capturing Alakeshvara alive together with his wife, children, and officials. When those who had seized He's ships heard of it, they returned to rescue them, and the imperial troops again dealt them a crushing defeat. In the sixth month of the ninth year he presented the prisoners at court. The emperor pardoned them and did not execute them, but released them and sent them home. At that time Jiaozhi had already been conquered and turned into commanderies and counties; the various states were even more alarmed and awed, and those who came increased daily.
5
十年十一月，復命和等往使，至蘇門答剌。 其前偽王子蘇幹剌者，方謀弒主自立，怒和賜不及己，率兵邀擊官軍。 和力戰，追擒之喃渤利，並俘其妻子，以十三年七月還朝。 帝大喜，賚諸將士有差。
In the eleventh month of the tenth year He was again ordered to go as envoy, reaching Samudra. The former pretender-prince Suganla was plotting to murder his lord and seize power; angered that He had not included him in the gifts, he led troops to intercept and attack the imperial army. He fought fiercely, pursued and captured Nanbuli, and took his wife and children prisoner, returning to court in the seventh month of the thirteenth year. The emperor was greatly pleased and gave the generals and soldiers rewards in due rank.
6
十四年冬，滿剌加、古裏等十九國咸遣使朝貢，辭還。 復命和等偕往，賜其君長。 十七年七月還。 十九年春復往，明年八月還。 二十二年正月，舊港酋長施濟孫請襲宣慰使職，和賫敕印往賜之。 比還，而成祖已晏駕。 洪熙元年二月，仁宗命和以下番諸軍守備南京。 南京設守備，自和始也。 宣德五年六月，帝以踐阼歲久，而諸番國遠者猶未朝貢，於是和、景弘復奉命歷忽魯謨斯等十七國而還。
In the winter of the fourteenth year, Melaka, Kuli, and nineteen other states all sent envoys to court and then took their leave. He was again ordered to go with them and bestow gifts on their rulers. They returned in the seventh month of the seventeenth year. In the spring of the nineteenth year they went again, and returned in the eighth month of the next year. In the first month of the twenty-second year, the chief of Jiu'gang, Shi Jisun, requested to inherit the office of Pacification Commissioner; He carried the imperial edict and seal to bestow it on him. By the time he returned, Chengzu had already died. In the second month of the first year of Hongxi, the emperor ordered He and the other maritime forces to guard Nanjing. The Nanjing guard began with He. In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuande, because the emperor had been on the throne for a long time and the distant states still had not come to offer tribute, He and Jinghong were again ordered to travel through seventeen states including Hulusimasi and return.
7
和經事三朝，先後七奉使，所歷占城、爪哇、真臘、舊港、暹羅、古裏、滿剌加、渤泥、蘇門答剌、阿魯、柯枝、大葛蘭、小葛蘭、西洋瑣裏、瑣裏、加異勒、阿撥把丹、南巫裏、甘把裏、錫蘭山、喃渤利、彭亨、急蘭丹、忽魯謨斯、比剌、溜山、孫剌、木骨都束、麻林、剌撒、祖法兒、沙裏灣泥、竹步、榜葛剌、天方、黎伐、那孤兒，凡三十餘國。 所取無名寶物，不可勝計，而中國耗廢亦不貲。 自宣德以還，遠方時有至者，要不如永樂時，而和亦老且死。 自和後，凡將命海表者，莫不盛稱和以誇外番，故俗傳三保太監下西洋，為明初盛事云。
He served under three reigns and was sent out seven times; the places he visited included Champa, Java, Chenla, Jiu'gang, Siam, Kuli, Melaka, Brunei, Samudra, Aru, Cochin, Great Calicut, Little Calicut, Western Ocean Suoli, Suoli, Jiayile, Ababadan, Nanwuli, Ganbali, Ceylon, Nanbuli, Pahang, Kelantan, Hormuz, Billa, Liushan, Sunla, Mogadishu, Malindi, Lasa, Zafar, Shaliwanni, Jubu, Bengal, Tianfang, Leifa, Naguer, and more than thirty states in all. The treasures he obtained were beyond counting, but China too suffered heavy expense. From the Xuande reign onward, people from distant regions sometimes came, but on the whole not as many as in Yongle's time, and He also grew old and died. After He, anyone sent on missions to the seas always boasted of He to foreign states; thus the common saying that the Three-Bao eunuch went down to the Western Ocean has long been counted as one of the great achievements of the early Ming.
8
當成祖時，銳意通四夷，奉使多用中貴。 西洋則和、景弘，西域則李達，迤北則海童，而西番則率使侯顯。
During Chengzu's reign, he was intent on reaching the four quarters, and those sent on missions were mostly inner officials. To the Western Ocean went He and Jinghong; to the Western Regions, Li Da; to the north, Haitong; and to the Western Barbarians, Huo Xian was generally sent.
9
侯顯者，司禮少監。 帝聞烏思藏僧尚師哈立麻有道術，善幻化，欲致一見，因通迤西諸番。 乃命顯賫書幣往迓，選壯士健馬護行。 元年四月奉使，陸行數萬里，至四年十二月始與其僧偕來，詔駙馬都尉沐昕迎之。 帝延見奉天殿，寵賚優渥，儀仗鞍馬什器多以金銀為之，道路烜赫。 五年二月建普度大齋於靈谷寺，為高帝、高後薦福。 或言卿雲、天花、甘露、甘雨、青鳥、青獅、白象、白鶴及舍利祥光，連日畢見，又聞梵唄天樂自空而下。 帝益大喜，廷臣表賀，學士胡廣等咸獻《聖孝瑞應歌》詩。 乃封哈立麻萬行具足十方最勝圓覺妙智慧善普應祐國演教如來大寶法王西天大善自在佛，領天下釋教，給印誥制如諸王，其徒三人亦封灌頂大國師，再宴奉天殿。 顯以奉使勞，擢太監。
Hou Xian. Hou Xian was the deputy director of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service. The emperor heard that the monk Shangshi Halima of U-Tsang possessed spiritual arts and could transform things, and wanted to meet him, thereby opening communication with the western states. So he ordered Xian to carry letters and gifts to invite him, and selected strong soldiers and sturdy horses to escort the journey. In the fourth month of the first year he received the mission; he traveled overland for tens of thousands of li and only in the twelfth month of the fourth year did he finally arrive together with the monk, whereupon an edict ordered the imperial son-in-law Mu Xin to receive him. The emperor received him in Fengtian Hall and showered him with generous gifts; the ceremonial banners, saddles, horses, and utensils were mostly made of gold and silver, and the roads shone with splendor. In the second month of the fifth year, a great Buddhist fasting rite was established at Linggu Temple to pray for blessings for the High Emperor and Empress Dowager. It was said that auspicious signs such as clouds of good omen, heavenly flowers, sweet dew, sweet rain, blue birds, blue lions, white elephants, white cranes, and relic light all appeared day after day, and they also heard Buddhist chant and heavenly music descending from the sky. The emperor was even more delighted; court ministers submitted congratulations, and the Hanlin academicians Hu Guang and others all offered the poem Sacred Filial Auspicious Response Song. He was then granted an enormously grand title and enfeoffed as the Great Treasure Dharma King of the Western Heaven, given authority over all Buddhism under heaven and granted seals and patents like the princes; his three disciples were also enfeoffed as Great National Masters of Empowerment, and they were banqueted again in Fengtian Hall. Because of his service on the mission, Xian was promoted to eunuch.
10
十一年春復奉命，賜西番尼八剌、地湧塔二國。 尼八剌王沙的新葛遣使隨顯入朝，表貢方物。 詔封國王，賜誥印。 十三年七月，帝欲通榜葛剌諸國，復命顯率舟師以行，其國即東印度之地，去中國絕遠。 其王賽佛丁遣使貢麒麟及諸方物。 帝大悅，錫予有加。 榜葛剌之西，有國曰沼納樸兒者，地居五印度中，古佛國也，侵榜葛剌。 賽佛丁告於朝。 十八年九月命顯往宣諭，賜金幣，遂罷兵。 宣德二年二月復使顯賜諸番，遍歷烏斯藏、必力工瓦、靈藏、思達藏諸國而還。 途遇寇劫，督將士力戰，多所斬獲。 還朝，錄功升賞者四百六十餘人。
In the spring of the eleventh year he again received orders, and was given gifts to bestow on the Western states of Nibala and Diyongta. The king of Nibala, Shadenige, sent envoys with Xian to court and present tribute of local products. An edict ordered him enfeoffed as king and given a patent and seal. In the seventh month of the thirteenth year, the emperor wanted to communicate with the states of Bengal and others, and again ordered Xian to lead a fleet there; that country was in eastern India, extremely far from China. Its king, Saifuding, sent envoys offering qilin and various local products. The emperor was greatly pleased and added to the rewards. West of Bengal there was a country called Zhaonapuer, located in the middle of the Five Indies and an ancient Buddhist country; it had invaded Bengal. Saifuding reported it to the court. In the ninth month of the eighteenth year Xian was ordered to go and announce this and pacify them; he bestowed gold and valuables, and the troops were then withdrawn. In the second month of Xuande's second year, Xian was again sent to bestow gifts on the foreign states, traveling through U-Tsang, Biligongwa, Lingzang, Sidazang, and the other countries before returning. On the way they encountered bandits, and he directed the generals and soldiers in a fierce battle, killing and capturing many. On return to court, more than four hundred and sixty men were recorded for merit promotion and reward.
11
顯有才辨，強力敢任，五使絕域，勞績與鄭和亞。
Xian was eloquent, strong, and bold in taking responsibility; on five missions to distant lands, his achievements were second only to Zheng He.
12
金英
Jin Ying
13
金英者，宣宗朝司禮太監也，親信用事。 宣德七年賜英及範弘免死詔，辭極褒美。 英宗立，與興安並貴幸。 及王振擅權，英不敢與抗。 正統十四年夏旱，命英理刑部、都察院獄囚，築壇大理寺。 英張黃蓋中坐，尚書以下左右列坐。 自是六年一審錄，制皆如此。 其秋，英宗北狩，中外大震。 郕王使英、安等召廷臣問計。 侍讀徐呈倡議南遷，安叱之，令扶呈出，大言曰：「敢言遷者斬！ 」遂入告太后，勸郕王任于謙治戰守。 或曰叱呈者，英也。
Jin Ying served as the eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial under the Xuande emperor and was personally trusted. In the seventh year of Xuande, an amnesty exempting Ying and Fan Hong from death was issued, and it praised them lavishly. When the Yingzong emperor ascended the throne, he and Xing'an were both powerful and favored. By the time Wang Zhen monopolized power, Ying did not dare contend with him. In the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, there was a drought; Ying was ordered to handle prisoners in the Ministry of Justice and Censorate, and an altar was erected at Dali Temple. Ying sat beneath a yellow canopy; ministers and those below sat on the left and right. From then on there was a review every six years, and the system was established thus. That autumn the Yingzong emperor was captured in the north, and the court and the provinces were thrown into great alarm. Prince Cheng sent Ying, An, and others to summon the court ministers and ask what to do. Reading Attendant Xu Cheng proposed moving the court south; An shouted at him, ordered that Xu Cheng be dragged out, and loudly declared: Anyone who dares speak of moving shall be executed! Then he went in to inform the Empress Dowager and urged the Prince of Cheng to entrust Yu Qian with the defense of war and strategy. Some said that Ying was the one who shouted at Xu Cheng.
14
也先入寇，至德勝門，景帝敕安與李永昌同于謙、石亨總理軍務。 永昌，亦司禮近侍也。 景泰元年十一月，英犯贓罪，下獄論死。 帝令禁錮之，終景帝世廢不用，獨任安。 也先遣使議和，請迎上皇，廷議報使。 帝不懌，令安出，呼群臣曰：「公等欲報使，孰可者？ 孰為文天祥、富弼！ 」詞色俱厲。 尚書王直面折之，安語塞。 及遣都給事中李寔往，敕書不及迎上皇。 寔驚，走白內閣，遇安。 安復詬曰：「若奉黃紙詔行耳，他何預！ 」及易儲諸，人遂疑安預謀矣。
When Esen invaded and reached Desheng Gate, the Jingtai Emperor ordered An and Li Yongchang, together with Yu Qian and Shi Heng, to oversee military affairs. Yongchang, too, was a close attendant in the Directorate of Ceremonial Service. In the eleventh month of the first year of Jingtai, Ying was charged with a corruption offense, imprisoned, and sentenced to death. The emperor ordered him confined; for the rest of Jingtai's reign he was set aside and not used, with An alone remaining in favor. Esen sent envoys to negotiate peace and requested the return of the retired emperor; the court debated how to answer. The emperor was displeased, sent An out, and summoned the ministers, saying: Gentlemen, if you wish to send a reply envoy, who would be suitable? Who could be a Wen Tianxiang or a Fu Bi? His words and expression were both severe. Minister Wang Zhi rebuked him to his face, and An had nothing more to say. When Assistant Censor Li Shi was sent, the imperial rescript did not mention bringing back the retired emperor. Shi was alarmed and hurried to report it to the Grand Secretariat, where he ran into An. An cursed him again, saying that he only needed to carry out the Yellow Paper edict and that nothing else mattered to him. When the succession was altered, people therefore suspected that An had been involved in the plot.
15
安有廉操，且知于謙賢，力護之。 或言帝任謙太過，安曰：「為國分憂如于公者，寧有二人！」
An had an upright character, and because he knew Yu Qian was worthy, he protected him vigorously. When some said the emperor trusted Qian too much, An replied: There cannot be two men like Yu Gong who share the state's burdens!

英宗復辟，蓋磔景帝所用太監王誠、舒良、張永、王勤等，謂其與黃厷構邪議，易太子，且與于謙、王文謀立外藩。 於是給事、御史皆言安與誠、良等為黨，宜同罪。 帝宥之，但奪職。 是時，中官坐誅者甚眾，安僅獲免云。 安佞佛，臨歿，遺命舂骨為灰，以供浮屠。
When Yingzong was restored, he had the eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, Wang Qin, and others who had served the Jingtai Emperor torn to pieces, saying they had joined Huang Gong in plotting evil schemes, changing the crown prince, and conspiring with Yu Qian and Wang Wen to install a prince from outside the court. Then the assistant secretaries and censors all said that An and Cheng, Liang, and the others were of one party and should be punished together. The emperor pardoned him, but stripped him of office. At that time many palace eunuchs were executed, and An alone barely escaped, it is said. An was devoutly Buddhist, and as he lay dying he left instructions that his bones be pounded to ash for an offering to the Buddha.

范弘，交阯人，初名安。 永樂中，英國公張輔以交童之美秀者還，選為奄，弘及王瑾、阮安、阮浪等與焉。 占對嫻雅，成祖愛之，教令讀書，涉經史，善筆劄，侍仁宗東宮。 宣德初，為更名，累遷司禮太監，偕英受免死詔，又偕英及御用太監王瑾同賜銀記。 正統時，英宗眷弘，嘗目之曰蓬來吉士。 十四年從征，歿於土木，喪歸，葬香山水安寺，弘建也。 而王瑾至景泰時始卒。
Fan Hong. Fan Hong was a man of Jiaozhi; his original name was An. During Yongle, Duke of England Zhang Fu returned with the handsome and promising boys of Jiaozhi and selected them to become eunuchs; Hong, Wang Jin, Ruan An, Ruan Lang, and others were among them. He answered questions with ease and elegance. Chengzu loved him, had him taught to read, let him study the Classics and Histories, and found him skilled with brush and writing; he served in the Eastern Palace of the Renzong Emperor. At the start of Xuande, he was given a new name, repeatedly promoted to eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, received an amnesty from death together with Ying, and later, together with Ying and the imperial-use eunuch Wang Jin, was also granted a silver tally. During Zhengtong, the Yingzong Emperor favored Hong and once called him a lucky man from Penglai. In the fourteenth year he followed the campaign and died at Tumu; his remains were brought home and buried at Shui'an Temple on Xiangshan, which Hong had built. Wang Jin, by contrast, died only in the Jingtai period.
18
瑾，初名陳蕪。 宣宗為皇太孫時，朝夕給事。 及即位，賜姓名。 從征漢王高煦還，參預四方兵事，賞賚累巨萬，數賜銀記曰「忠肝義膽」，曰「金貂貴客」，曰「忠誠自勵」，曰「心跡雙清」。 又賜以兩宮人，官其養子王椿。 其受寵眷，英、弘莫逮也。
Jin's original name was Chen Wu. When the future Xuanzong was crown prince grandson, he served him morning and evening. When he came to the throne, he gave him a new name. After returning from the campaign against Prince Han Gao Xu, he was involved in military affairs in every quarter, received rewards amounting to many tens of thousands, and was repeatedly given silver tallies bearing the inscriptions Loyal Liver, Righteous Gall, Golden Marten, Noble Guest, Loyal Self-Encouragement, and Heart and Conduct Both Pure. He was also given two palace women, and his adopted son Wang Chun was made an official. In the favor he received, neither Ying nor Hong could match him.
19
阮安有巧思，奉成祖命營北京城池宮殿及百司府廨，目量意營，悉中規制，工部奉行而已。 正統時，重建三殿，治楊村河，並有功。 景泰中，治張秋河，道卒，囊無十金。
Ruan An had inventive skill. By Chengzu's order he planned Beijing's walls, palaces, and the offices of the hundred departments; measuring by eye and working from his own design, he made everything conform to regulation, and the Ministry of Works merely carried it out. In Zhengtong, he rebuilt the Three Halls and managed the Yangcun River, and had merit in both. In Jingtai, while managing the Zhangqiu River, he died on the road, with less than ten in his purse.

阮浪至景帝時，為御用監少監。 英宗居南宮，浪入侍，賜鍍金繡袋及鍍金刀。 浪以贈門下皇城使王瑤。 錦衣衛指揮盧忠者，險人也，見瑤袋刀異常制，醉瑤而竊之，以告尚衣監高平。 平令校尉李善上變，言浪傳上皇命，以袋刀結瑤謀復位。 景帝下浪、瑤詔獄，忠證之，浪、瑤皆磔死，詞終不及上皇。 英宗復辟，磔忠及平，而贈浪太監。
By the Jingtai Emperor's time, Ruan Lang was deputy director of the Imperial Use Office. When Yingzong was in the Southern Palace, Lang attended him and was given a gilded embroidered pouch and a gilded knife. Lang gave them to Wang Yao, a gate attendant of the imperial city. Lu Zhong, commander of the Brocade Guard, was a treacherous man; seeing that Yao's pouch and knife were of an unusual pattern, he got Yao drunk, stole them, and reported the matter to Gao Ping of the Wardrobe Office. Gao Ping ordered the sergeant Li Shan to file a denunciation, saying Lang had transmitted the retired emperor's order and used the pouch and knife to win over Yao in a plot to restore the throne. The Jingtai Emperor sent Lang and Yao to the imperial prison; Zhong testified against them, and Lang and Yao were both torn to death, though their statements never mentioned the retired emperor. When Yingzong was restored, Zhong and Ping were torn to death, and Lang was posthumously made eunuch.
21
王振，蔚州人。 少選入內書堂。 侍英宗東宮，為局郎。 初，太祖禁中官預政。 自永樂後，漸加委寄，然犯法輒置極典。 宣宗時，袁琦令阮巨隊等出外采辦。 事覺，琦磔死，巨隊等皆斬。 又裴可烈等不法，立誅之。 諸中官以是不敢肆。 及英宗立，年少。 振狡黠得帝歡，遂越金英等數人掌司禮監，導帝用重典禦下，防大臣欺蔽。 於是大臣下獄者不絕，而振得因以市權。 然是時，太皇太后賢，方委政內閣。 閣臣楊士奇、楊榮、楊溥，皆累朝元老，振心憚之未敢逞。 至正統七年，太皇太后崩，榮已先卒，士奇以子稷論死不出，溥老病，新閣臣馬愉、曹鼐勢輕，振遂跋扈不可制。 作大第皇城東，建智化寺，窮極土木。 興麓川之師，西南騷動。 侍講劉球因雷震上言陳得失，語刺振。 振下球獄，使指揮馬順支解之。 大理少卿薛瑄、祭酒李時勉素不禮振。 振摭他事陷瑄幾死，時勉至荷校國子監門。 御史李鐸遇振不跪，謫戍鐵嶺衛。 駙馬都尉石璟詈其家閹，振惡賤己同類，下璟獄。 怒霸州知州張需禁飭牧馬校卒，逮之，並坐需舉主王鐸。 又械戶部尚書劉中敷，侍郎吳璽、陳常於長安門。 所忤恨，輒加罪謫。 內侍張環、顧忠、錦衣衛卒王永心不平，以匿名書暴振罪狀。 事發，磔於市，不覆奏。
Wang Zhen. Wang Zhen was a man of Weizhou. He was selected young and entered the inner school hall. He served in the Eastern Palace of the Yingzong Emperor as a bureau attendant. At first, the Ming founder forbade palace eunuchs from taking part in government. After Yongle, they were gradually entrusted with more responsibilities, but whenever they broke the law, they were punished with the harshest penalties. During the Xuanzong reign, Yuan Qi sent Ruan Judui and others outside to procure goods. When the matter came to light, Qi was torn to death and Judui and the others were all beheaded. When Pei Kelie and others also acted unlawfully, they were executed at once. Because of this, the palace eunuchs did not dare to run wild. When Yingzong ascended the throne, he was still young. Zhen, crafty and sly, won the emperor's favor and was thus put over Jin Ying and several others to run the Directorate of Ceremonial Service; he led the emperor to use harsh laws to control his subordinates and guard against ministers' deceit and concealment. Thereafter, ministers were sent to prison without end, and Zhen used the situation to barter for power. But at this time the Grand Empress Dowager was capable and was entrusting power to the Grand Secretariat. The Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi, Yang Rong, and Yang Pu were all veteran ministers across several reigns, and Zhen feared them in his heart and did not dare act freely. By the seventh year of Zhengtong, the Grand Empress Dowager died; Rong had already passed away, Shiqi stayed home because his son Ji had been condemned to death, Pu was old and ill, and the new Grand Secretaries Ma Yu and Cao Nai were weak in power, so Zhen became overbearing and uncontrollable. He built a vast mansion east of the imperial city and constructed Zhihua Temple, exhausting all the resources of labor and wood. He launched the campaign against Luchuan, and the southwest was thrown into turmoil. The attending lecturer Liu Qiu used a thunderstorm as the occasion to submit a memorial laying out merits and faults; his words were aimed at Zhen. Zhen had Qiu thrown into prison and ordered Commander Ma Shun to dismember him. Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Xue Xuan and Administrator Li Shimian had long shown Zhen no respect. Zhen seized on other matters to implicate Xuan and nearly kill him; Shimian was made to wear the cangue at the gate of the National Academy. When the censor Li Duo met Zhen, he did not kneel; he was demoted to garrison service at Tieling Guard. The imperial son-in-law Shi Jing cursed the eunuch in his household; Zhen hated his insulting one of his own kind and had Jing imprisoned. Angered that Zhang Xu, magistrate of Bazhou, had restrained the horse grooms and drillers, he had Zhang arrested and also implicated Xu's recommender, Wang Duo. He also had Minister of Revenue Liu Zhongfu and the vice ministers Wu Xi and Chen Chang bound in shackles at Chang'an Gate. Anyone who offended or enraged him was at once punished and exiled. The inner attendants Zhang Huan and Gu Zhong and the Brocade Guard soldier Wang Yong, unable to bear it, exposed Zhen's crimes in an anonymous letter. When the matter came to light, they were torn to death in the market, without further report to the throne.
22
帝方傾心向振，嘗以先生呼之。 賜振敕，極褒美。 振權日益積重，公侯勛戚呼曰翁父。 畏禍者爭附振免死，賕賂輳集。 工部郎中王祐以善諂擢本部侍郎，兵部尚書徐晞等多至屈膝。 其從子山、林至蔭都督指揮。 私黨馬順、郭敬、陳官、唐童等並肆行無忌。 久之，構釁瓦剌，振遂敗。 瓦剌者，元裔也。 十四年，其太師也先貢馬，振減其直，使者恚而去。 秋七月，也先大舉入寇，振挾帝親征。 廷臣交諫，弗聽。 至宣府，大風雨，復有諫者，振益虓怒。 成國公朱勇等白事，咸膝行進。 尚書鄺埜、王佐忤振意，罰跪草中。 其黨欽天監正彭德清以天象諫，振終弗從。 八月己酉，帝駐大同，振益欲北。 鎮守太監郭敬以敵勢告，振始懼。 班師，至雙寨，雨甚。 振初議道紫荊關，由蔚州邀帝幸其第，既恐蹂鄉稼，復改道宣府。 軍士紆回奔走，壬戌始次土木。 瓦剌兵追至，師大潰。 帝蒙塵，振乃為亂兵所殺。 敗報聞，百官慟哭，都御史陳鎰等廷奏振罪，給事中王竑等立擊殺馬順及毛、王二中官。 郕王命臠王山於市，並振黨誅之，振族無少長皆斬。 振擅權七年，籍其家，得金銀六十餘庫，玉盤百，珊瑚高六七尺者二十餘株，他珍玩無算。 先是，郭敬鎮大同，幾造箭鏃數十甕，以振命遺瓦剌，瓦剌輒報以良馬。 及帝親征，西寧侯宋瑛、駙馬都尉井源為前鋒，遇敵陽和，敬又撓使敗。 至是逃歸，亦坐誅。
The emperor was then wholly devoted to Zhen and had once addressed him as Sir. He bestowed an imperial rescript on Zhen with extravagant praise. Zhen's power grew heavier by the day, and dukes, marquises, and meritorious kin all called him Father-in-law. Those who feared calamity rushed to attach themselves to Zhen to escape death, and bribes poured in from every side. Wang You, a clerk in the Ministry of Works, was promoted to vice minister by dint of flattery, and Minister of War Xu Xi and the others often went so far as to kneel before him. His nephews Shan and Lin were granted offices as Guard commanders. His private allies, Ma Shun, Guo Jing, Chen Guan, Tang Tong, and others, all ran wild without restraint. After a long time he provoked the Oirats, and Zhen was defeated. The Oirats were descendants of the Yuan. In the fourteenth year, their taishi Esen presented horses; Zhen reduced their price, and the envoy left in anger. In the seventh month of autumn, Esen launched a major invasion, and Zhen took the emperor on a personal expedition. The court ministers repeatedly remonstrated, but he would not listen. When they reached Xuanfu, fierce winds and rain arose, and when more people remonstrated, Zhen became even more savage and furious. When Duke Chengguo Zhu Yong and the others came to report business, they all advanced on their knees. Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo offended Zhen's wishes and were punished by kneeling in the grass. His ally Peng Deqing, Director of the Astronomical Bureau, remonstrated with him on the basis of the celestial omens, but Zhen still would not follow him. On the jiyou day of the eighth month, the emperor was camped at Datong, and Zhen was determined even more to press north. The eunuch in charge of garrison affairs, Guo Jing, reported the strength of the enemy, and Zhen finally became afraid. When the army began its return march, it reached Shuangzhai in heavy rain. At first Zhen planned to take the Zijing Pass route and bring the emperor by way of Wei Prefecture to visit his own residence, but fearing that this would trample the villages' crops, he again changed course to Xuanfu. The soldiers had to take long detours and hurry about, and only on the renxu day did they reach Tumubao. The Oirat troops pursued them there, and the army was utterly routed. The emperor was taken captive, and Zhen was then killed by the rebel troops. When the news of the defeat arrived, all the officials wailed aloud; the Grand Censor Chen Yi and others presented Zhen's crimes at court, and the Assistant Secretaries Wang Hong and others immediately struck down and killed Ma Shun and the two eunuchs Mao and Wang. The Prince of Cheng ordered Wang Shan to be quartered in the market and had Zhen's party executed; all of Zhen's clan, young and old, were beheaded. Zhen monopolized power for seven years; when his household was confiscated, they found more than sixty chests of gold and silver, a hundred jade dishes, more than twenty corals six or seven chi high, and countless other rare treasures and curios. Earlier, when Guo Jing was stationed at Datong, he had made nearly several dozen urns of arrowheads and sent them to the Oirats on Zhen's orders, and the Oirats always replied with fine horses. When the emperor led the campaign himself, the Marquis of Xining, Song Ying, and the imperial son-in-law Jing Yuan served as the vanguard; when they met the enemy at Yanghe, Guo Jing again thwarted them and caused their defeat. When he fled back this time, he too was executed.
23
英宗復辟，顧念振不置。 用太監劉恒言，賜振祭，招魂以葬，祀之智化寺，賜祠曰精忠。 而振門下曹吉祥復以奪門功，有寵顓政。
When Yingzong was restored, he still remembered Zhen and could not let him go. Using the eunuch Liu Heng's suggestion, he granted Zhen sacrificial offerings, summoned his soul for burial, honored him at Zhihua Temple, and bestowed on the shrine the title Perfect Loyalty. Meanwhile, Zhen's retainer Cao Jixiang, having won favor through the seizure of the gates, also monopolized power.
24
曹吉祥
Cao Jixiang
25
曹吉祥，灤州人。 素依王振。 正統初，征麓川，為監軍。 征兀良哈，與成國公朱勇、太監劉永誠分道。 又與寧陽侯陳懋等征鄧茂七於福建，吉祥每出，輒選達官、跳蕩卒隸帳下，師還畜於家，故家多藏甲。
Cao Jixiang came from Luanzhou. He had long relied on Wang Zhen. At the start of Zhengtong, when the campaign against Luchuan was launched, he served as supervising officer. In the campaign against Wuliangha, he took a separate route with Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and the eunuch Liu Yongcheng. He also campaigned with the Marquis of Ningyang, Chen Mao, against Deng Maoqi in Fujian; whenever Jixiang went out, he would pick able officers and assault troops to attach to his tent, and when the army returned he kept them at home, so his household contained many hidden weapons.
26
景泰中，分掌京營。 後與石亨結，帥兵迎英宗復位。 遷司禮太監，總督三大營。 嗣子欽，從子鉉、鐸等皆官都督，欽進封昭武伯，門下廝養冒官者多至千百人，朝士亦有依附希進者，權勢與石亨埒，時並稱曹、石。 二人惡言官有言，共譖於帝，命吏部尚書王翺察核年三十五以上者留，不及者調用。 於是給事何玘等十三人改州判官，御史吳禎等二十三人改知縣。 會有風雷雨雹之變，帝乃悟，悉還其職。 未幾，二人爭寵有隙，御史楊瑄、張鵬劾之，吉祥乃復與亨合，乘間醞帝。 帝為下瑄等詔獄，而逮治閣臣徐有貞、李賢等。 事具賢傳。 承天門災，帝命閣臣嶽正草罪己詔，詔語激切。 吉祥、亨復正謗訕，帝又謫正。 焰益張，朝野仄目。
In the Jingtai reign, he was put in joint charge of the capital garrisons. Later he allied with Shi Heng and led troops to bring the Yingzong Emperor back to the throne. He was promoted to eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service and put in overall command of the Three Great Garrisons. His adopted son Qin and his nephews Xuan and Quan were all made guard commanders; Qin was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaowu, and his household retainers who had assumed official rank numbered in the hundreds and thousands. Some court officials also attached themselves to him in hopes of advancement, and his power and influence matched Shi Heng's, so they were known together as Cao and Shi. The two disliked officials speaking out, and together slandered them before the emperor. The emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Wang Ao to investigate and verify those aged thirty-five and above, who were to remain, while those below that age were to be reassigned. As a result, thirteen men including the assistant secretary He Qi were transferred to posts as prefectural vice-magistrates, and twenty-three censors including Wu Zhen were transferred to serve as county magistrates. Then a change of wind, thunder, rain, and hail occurred, and the emperor awakened to the situation and restored all of them to office. Not long after, the two fell out over competition for favor; the censors Yang Xuan and Zhang Peng impeached them, and Jixiang once again allied with Heng and took advantage of the opening to make the emperor intoxicated. The emperor had Xuan and the others sent to the imperial prison, and also had the Grand Secretariat ministers Xu Youzhen, Li Xian, and others taken into custody and investigated. The details are given in Li Xian's biography. When the fire at Cheng Tian Gate broke out, the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Yue Zheng to draft an edict of self-reproach, and the language of the edict was intense and forceful. Jixiang and Heng again had Zheng slander and vilify others, and the emperor again demoted Zheng. Their flames grew ever fiercer, and both court and country looked on in dread.
27
久之，帝覺其奸，意稍稍疑。 及李賢力言奪門非是，始大悟，疏吉祥。 無何，石亨敗，吉祥不自安，漸蓄異謀，日犒諸達官，金錢、穀帛恣所取。 諸達官恐吉祥敗而己隨黜退也，皆願盡力效死。 欽問客馮益曰：「自古有宦官子弟為天子者乎？ 」益曰：「君家魏武，其人也。 」欽大喜。 天順五年七月，欽私掠家人曹福來，為言官所劾。 帝令錦衣指揮逮杲按之，降敕遍諭群臣。 欽驚曰：「前降敕，遂捕石將軍。 今復爾，殆矣。 」謀遂決。 是時甘、涼告警，帝命懷寧侯孫鏜西征，未發。 吉祥使其黨掌欽天監太常少卿湯序擇是月庚子昧爽，欽擁兵入，而已以禁軍應之。 謀定，欽召諸達官夜飲。 是夜，鏜及恭順侯吳瑾俱宿朝房。 達官馬亮恐事敗，逸出，走告瑾。 瑾趣鏜由長安右門隙投疏入。 帝急縶吉祥於內，而敕皇城及京城九門閉弗啟。 欽知亮逸，中夜馳往逮杲家，殺杲，斫傷李賢於東朝房。 以杲頭示賢曰：「杲激我也。 」又殺都御史寇深於西朝房。 攻東、西長安門不得入，縱火。 守衛者拆河壖磚石塞諸門。 賊往來叫呼門外。 鏜遣二子急召西征軍擊欽於東長安門。 欽走攻東安門，道殺瑾。 復縱火，門毀。 門內聚薪益之，火熾，賊不得入。 天漸曙，欽黨稍稍散去。 鏜勒兵逐欽，斬鉉、鐸，鏜子軏斫欽中膊。 欽走突安定諸門，門盡閉。 奔歸家，拒戰。 會大雨如註，鏜督諸軍大呼入，欽投井死。 遂殺鐸，盡屠其家。 越三日，磔吉祥於市。 湯序、馮益及吉祥姻黨皆伏誅。 馬亮以告反者，授都督。
After a long while, the emperor perceived their treachery and began to suspect them. When Li Xian strongly argued that the gate seizure was wrong, he finally awakened fully and distanced himself from Jixiang. Not long after, Shi Heng was defeated, and Jixiang, no longer at ease, gradually harbored rebel schemes; each day he rewarded the various inner officers, letting them take gold, money, grain, and silk as they wished. The various inner officers feared that if Jixiang failed, they too would be dismissed and demoted, and so all were willing to do their utmost and die for him. Qin asked the guest Feng Yi: "From antiquity, has there been a son of a eunuch who became emperor?" Yi replied: "Your house's Wei Wu is that man." Qin was greatly pleased. In the seventh month of the fifth year of Tianshun, Qin privately seized the household servant Cao Fulai, and was impeached by the remonstrance officials. The emperor ordered a Brocade Guard commander to seize Gao and investigate the matter, and issued an edict that was circulated to all the ministers. Qin was alarmed and said: "With the last edict, they went and arrested General Shi. If this happens again now, we are finished." The plan was then decided. At that time Gansu and Liangzhou sent alarm reports, and the emperor ordered Marquis of Huaining Sun Tang to campaign west, but he had not yet departed. Jixiang had his ally, the Vice Minister of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau and Directorate of Sacrifices, Tang Xu, choose the pre-dawn of the gengzi day of that month; Qin would enter with his troops, and he himself would answer with the forbidden army. Once the plan was set, Qin summoned the various inner officers for a night of drinking. That night, Tang and the Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Jin, both stayed in the court lodging. The inner officer Ma Liang feared the plot would fail, escaped, and ran to tell Wu Jin. Wu Jin urged Tang to send a memorial through the gap at the right gate of Chang'an. The emperor quickly had Jixiang bound inside, and ordered the imperial city and all nine gates of the capital closed and not opened. When Qin learned that Liang had escaped, he rode out in the middle of the night to arrest Gao's household, killed Gao, and hacked Li Xian to pieces at the eastern court chamber. Holding Gao's head up to Li Xian, he said: "Gao provoked me." Then he also killed Grand Censor Kou Shen in the western court chamber. He attacked the east and west Chang'an Gates but could not break in, so he set them on fire. The guards tore up bricks and stones from the riverbank and blocked the gates with them. The rebels ran back and forth shouting outside the gates. Tang sent his two sons to urgently summon the western expedition army to strike Qin at the east Chang'an Gate. Qin ran to attack the east An Gate, and on the way killed Wu Jin. He again set fires, and the gate was destroyed. Within the gate, they piled firewood and added to it; the flames roared, and the rebels could not get in. As dawn gradually approached, Qin's followers began to disperse little by little. Tang led troops in pursuit of Qin, had Xuan and Quan beheaded, and Tang's son Yue hacked Qin in the shoulder. Qin fled to break through the gates of Anying and others, but all the gates were shut. He ran back home and put up a fight. Then a heavy rain fell in sheets; Tang directed the various armies to shout and charge in, and Qin threw himself into a well and died. They then killed Duo and massacred his whole family. Three days later, they tore Jixiang to pieces in the market. Tang Xu, Feng Yi, and all Jixiang's in-laws and party were likewise executed. Ma Liang, because he had reported the rebellion, was appointed a Guard commander.
28
英宗始任王振，繼任吉祥，凡兩致禍亂。 其他宦者若跛兒幹、亦失哈、喜寧、韋力轉、牛玉之屬，率凶狡。 土木之敗，跛兒幹、喜寧皆降敵。 跛兒幹助敵反攻，射內使黎定。 既又為敵使至京，有所需索，景帝執而誅之。 喜寧數為也先畫策，索賞賜，導入邊寇掠。 上皇患之，言於也先； 使寧還京索禮物，而命校尉袁彬以密書報邊臣。 至獨石，參將楊俊擒寧送京師，景泰元年二月磔於市。 亦失哈鎮遼東。 敵犯廣寧，亦失哈禁官軍勿出擊。 百戶施帶兒降敵，為脫脫不花通於亦失哈。 正統十四年冬，帶兒逃歸，巡按御史劉孜並劾亦失哈及他不法事。 景帝命誅帶兒，而置亦失哈不問。 韋力轉者，性淫毒，鎮守大同，多過惡。 銜軍妻不與宿，杖死其軍。 又與養子妻淫戲，射殺養子。 天順元年，工部侍郎霍瑄發力轉僭用金器若王者，及強娶所部女為妾諸不法事。 帝怒，執之下錦衣衛獄，既而宥之。 牛玉事，詳《吳廢後傳》。
Yingzong first relied on Wang Zhen and then on Jixiang, and the two together brought about disaster and disorder. Other eunuchs, such as Boer Gan, Yishihha, Xi Ning, Weilizhuan, and Niu Yu, were generally vicious and cunning. After the defeat at Tumu, Boer Gan and Xi Ning both surrendered to the enemy. Boer Gan helped the enemy counterattack and shot the inner attendant Li Ding. Later he also served as an envoy of the enemy to the capital, demanding things; the Jingtai Emperor seized and executed him. Xi Ning repeatedly plotted for Esen, demanded rewards, and led border troops to plunder. The retired emperor was troubled by him and spoke of it to Esen; he was sent back to the capital to demand gifts, and the sergeant Yuan Bin was ordered to send a secret letter to the border commanders. When he reached Dushi, the Assistant Commander Yang Jun captured Ning and sent him to the capital, where he was torn to pieces in the market in the second month of the first year of Jingtai. Yishihha was stationed in Liaodong. When the enemy attacked Guangning, Yishihha forbade the imperial troops from going out to strike back. The hundred-household officer Shi Daier surrendered to the enemy and became the go-between for Tuo Tuo Bu Hua and Yishihha. In the winter of the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, Daier fled back, and the surveillance censor Liu Zi impeached Yishihha and the other unlawful matters together. The Jingtai Emperor ordered Daier executed, but left Yishihha uninvestigated. Wei Lizhuan was licentious and vicious; when he was in charge at Datong, he committed many outrageous crimes. He slept with the wife of an army officer and, when she would not lie with him, had the man beaten to death. He also committed adultery and playing around with the wife of an adopted son and shot the adopted son dead. In the first year of Tianshun, the Ministry of Works vice minister Huo Xuan exposed Wei Lizhuan's unlawful acts, including using gold vessels like a king and forcibly taking women from the units under his command as concubines. The emperor was furious, had him arrested and sent to the Brocade Guard prison, then later pardoned him. The matter of Niu Yu is detailed in the Biography of Wu's Deposed Empress.

劉永誠
Liu Yongcheng
30
其與吉祥分道征兀良哈者劉永誠，永樂時，嘗為偏將，累從北征。 宣德、正統中，再擊兀良哈。 後監鎮甘、涼，戰沙漠，有功。 景泰末，掌團營。 英宗復辟，勒兵從，官其嗣子聚。 成化中，永誠始卒。
Liu Yongcheng, who went by a separate route with Jixiang against Wuliangha, had served as a deputy general in the Yongle reign and repeatedly joined northern expeditions. During Xuande and Zhengtong he again fought Wuliangha. Later he supervised and garrisoned Gansu and Liangzhou, where he fought in the desert and won merit. At the end of Jingtai he was put in charge of the group armies. When Yingzong was restored, he led troops in attendance, and his adopted son Ju was made an official. He died in the Chenghua reign.
31
懷恩，高密人，兵部侍郎戴綸族弟也。 宣宗殺綸，並籍恩父太僕卿希文家。 恩方幼，被宮為小黃門，賜名懷恩。 憲宗朝，掌司禮監。 時汪直理西廠，梁芳、韋興等用事。 恩班在前，性忠鯁無所撓，諸閹咸敬憚之。 員外郎林俊論芳及僧繼曉下獄，帝欲誅之，恩固爭。 帝怒，投以硯曰：「若助俊訕我。 」恩免冠伏地號哭。 帝叱之出。 恩遣人告鎮撫司曰：「汝曹諂芳傾俊。 俊死，汝曹何以生！ 」徑歸，稱疾不起。 帝怒解，遣醫視恩，卒釋俊。 會星變，罷諸傳奉官。 御馬監王敏請留馬房傳奉者，帝許之。 敏謁恩，恩大罵曰：「星變，專為我曹壞國政故。 今甫欲正之，又為汝壞，天雷擊汝矣！ 」敏愧恨，遂死。 進寶石者章瑾求為錦衣衛鎮撫，恩不可，曰：「鎮撫掌詔獄，奈何以賄進。 」當是時，尚書王恕以直諫名，恩每嘆曰：「天下忠義，斯人而已。 」憲宗末，惑萬貴妃言，欲易太子，恩固爭。 帝不懌，斥居鳳陽。 孝宗立，召歸，仍掌司禮監，力勸帝逐萬安，用王恕。 一時正人匯進，恩之力也。 卒，賜祠額曰顯忠。
Huai'en. Huai'en was a man of Gaomi and a clan younger brother of Dai Lun, vice minister of war. When Xuanzong killed Lun, he also confiscated the family of Huai'en's father Xiwen, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sheds. Huai'en was still young, and was taken into the palace as a small yellow gate attendant and given the name Huai'en. In the Chenghua reign he was in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service. At that time Wang Zhi was managing the Western Depot, while Liang Fang, Wei Xing, and others were in power. Huai'en held the lead rank, was loyal and outspoken without any bending, and all the eunuchs respected and feared him. When Assistant Minister Lin Jun impeached Fang and the monk Jixiao and was thrown into prison, the emperor wanted to execute him, but Huai'en strongly argued against it. The emperor grew angry and threw an inkstone at him, saying: "You are helping Jun slander me. Huai'en removed his cap, prostrated himself on the ground, and cried aloud. The emperor shouted at him to get out. Huai'en sent someone to tell the Commandery of Suppression: "You flatter Fang and bring Jun down. If Jun dies, how can you live?" He went straight home and claimed illness, refusing to rise. When the emperor's anger subsided, he sent a physician to examine Huai'en and ultimately released Jun. Then an astronomical anomaly occurred, and all the transmission-offering officials were dismissed. The imperial stable supervisor Wang Min requested that the transmission-offering men at the horse stables be retained, and the emperor granted it. When Min paid his respects to Huai'en, Huai'en cursed him savagely, saying: "The celestial anomaly happened because of us, to ruin the state. Now that we have only just tried to set things right, you have ruined them again; thunder from heaven will strike you!" Min was ashamed and resentful, and soon died. When Zhang Jin brought a precious stone and asked to become a Brocade Guard commander, Huai'en refused, saying: "A commander of suppression handles imperial prisons; how can he be advanced by bribery? At that time Minister Wang Shu was known for blunt remonstrance, and Huai'en often sighed: "Among the loyal and righteous under heaven, this man alone remains." At the end of the Chenghua reign, when the emperor was misled by Empress Wan's words and wanted to change the crown prince, Huai'en strongly argued against it. The emperor was displeased and banished him to Fengyang. When the Xiaozong Emperor ascended the throne, he recalled him and again put him in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, where he strongly urged the emperor to expel Wan An and use Wang Shu. The gathering of upright men at that time was due to Huai'en's efforts. When he died, the shrine was granted the plaque Distinguished Loyalty.

同時有覃吉者，不知所由進，以老閹侍太子。 太子年九歲，吉口授《四書》章句及古今政典。 憲宗賜太子莊田，吉勸毋受，曰：「天下皆太子有也。 」太子偶從內侍讀佛經，吉入，太子驚曰：「老伴來矣。 」亟手《孝經》。 吉跪曰：「太子誦佛書乎？ 」曰：「無有。 《孝經》耳。 」吉頓首曰：「甚善。 佛書誕，不可信也。 」弘治之世，政治醇美，君德清明，端本正始，吉有力焉。
Qin Ji. There was also a man named Qin Ji, and no one knew how he had risen, but as an old eunuch he served the crown prince. When the crown prince was nine years old, Ji orally taught him the chapters and verses of the Four Books and the political canons of ancient and modern times. When the Chenghua Emperor granted the crown prince estates, Ji urged him not to accept them, saying: "The whole realm already belongs to the crown prince." One day the crown prince was listening to a Buddhist sutra with an inner attendant when Ji entered; the crown prince, startled, said: "My old companion has come." He hurriedly pointed to the Classic of Filial Piety. Ji knelt and said: "Is the crown prince reciting a Buddhist text?" The crown prince replied: "No. The Classic of Filial Piety only." Ji bowed his head and said: "Excellent." Buddhist texts are absurd and not to be trusted." In the reign of Hongzhi, the government was pure and excellent, the ruler's virtue was clear, the root was set right, and the beginning was made correct; Ji contributed greatly to that.

汪直者，大藤峽瑤種也。 初給事萬貴妃於昭德宮，遷御馬監太監。 成化十二年，黑眚見宮中，妖人李子龍以符術結太監韋舍私入大內，事發，伏誅。 帝心惡之，銳欲知外事。 直為人便黠，帝因令易服，將校尉一二人密出伺察，人莫知也，獨都御史王越與結歡。 明年設西廠，以直領之，列官校刺事。 南京鎮監覃力朋進貢還，以百艘載私鹽，騷擾州縣。 武城縣典史詰之，力朋擊典史，折其齒，射殺一人。 直廉得以聞，逮治論斬。 力朋後得幸免，而帝以此謂直能摘奸，益幸直。 直乃任錦衣百戶韋瑛為心腹，屢興大獄。
Wang Zhi. Wang Zhi was a Yao of Dazuo Gorge. At first he attended Empress Wan in Zhaode Palace, then was promoted to eunuch of the Imperial Horse Directorate. In the twelfth year of Chenghua, a black omen appeared in the palace; the sorcerer Li Zilong used talismans to befriend the eunuch Wei She and secretly enter the inner palace, but when the matter was exposed, he was executed. The emperor came to dislike it and grew eager to know what was happening outside. Zhi was quick and cunning; the emperor therefore had him change clothes and, with one or two cavalry sergeants, secretly go out to observe and investigate, so that no one knew it, and only the Grand Censor Wang Yue became friendly with him. The next year the Western Depot was established and placed under Zhi, with a line of officials and guards sent out to spy on affairs. Qin Lipeng, the garrison supervisor of Nanjing, returned after delivering tribute and loaded a hundred boats with private salt, harassing the prefectures and counties. When the magistrate clerk of Wucheng County questioned him, Lipeng beat the clerk, broke his teeth, and shot one man dead. Zhi investigated and reported it; Lipeng was seized, tried, and sentenced to death by beheading. Lipeng later escaped punishment, and the emperor, seeing this as proof that Zhi could uncover criminals, favored Zhi even more. Zhi then took the Brocade Guard hundred-household officer Wei Ying as his trusted agent and repeatedly initiated major prosecutions.
34
建寧衛指揮楊曄，故少師榮曾孫也，與父泰為仇家所告，逃入京，匿姊夫董玙所。 玙為請瑛，瑛陽諾而馳報直。 直即捕曄、玙考訊，三琶之。 琶者，錦衣酷刑也。 骨節皆寸解，絕而復蘇。 曄不勝苦，妄言寄金於其叔父兵部主事士偉所。 直不復奏請，捕士偉下獄，並掠其妻孥。 獄具，曄死獄中，泰論斬，士偉等皆謫官，郎中武清、樂章，行人張廷綱，參政劉福等皆無故被收案。 自諸王府邊鎮及南北河道，所在校尉羅列，民間鬥詈雞狗瑣事，輒置重法，人情大擾。 直每出，隨從甚眾，公卿皆避道。 兵部尚書項忠不避，迫辱之，權焰出東廠上。
Yang Ye, commander of Jianning Guard, was a grandson of the former Grand Tutor Rong. He and his father Tai had been denounced by an enemy clan and fled to the capital, where they hid at his brother-in-law Dong Yu's home. Yu begged Wei Ying on his behalf; Wei Ying agreed on the surface but hurried to report it to Zhi. Zhi at once arrested Ye and Yu, interrogated them, and put them to the three tortures. The pa-luo was a brutal torture of the Brocade Guard. The joints were all dislocated joint by joint, and he would lose consciousness and then come back to life. Unable to endure the torture, Ye falsely said that he had stored gold with his uncle Shi Wei, a clerk in the Ministry of War. Zhi did not seek further report; he seized Shi Wei, imprisoned him, and also looted his wife and children. When the case was finished, Ye died in prison, Tai was sentenced to beheading, Shi Wei and the others were all demoted, and even officials like the langzhong Wuqing and Lezhang, the envoy Zhang Tinggang, and the vice minister Liu Fu were all falsely swept up in the case. From the border garrisons of the princely households to the north and south river routes, sergeants were stationed everywhere; even minor commoner disputes over dogs and chickens were often dealt with under harsh law, and public feeling was greatly disturbed. Whenever Zhi went out, he was followed by a great retinue, and all the nobles and ministers cleared the road for him. Minister of War Xiang Zhong did not avoid him, pushed and humiliated him, and his power and arrogance surpassed those of the Eastern Depot.
35
五月，大學士商輅與萬安、劉珝、劉吉奏其狀。 帝震怒，命司禮太監懷恩、覃吉、黃高至閣下，厲色傳旨，言：「疏出誰意？ 」輅口數直罪甚悉，因言：「臣等同心一意，為國除害，無有先後。 」珝慷慨泣下。 恩遂據實以奏。 頃之，傳旨慰勞。 翼日，尚書忠及諸大臣疏亦入。 帝不得已，罷西廠，使懷恩數直罪而宥之，令歸御馬監，調韋瑛邊衛，散諸旗校還錦衣。 中外大悅。 然帝眷直不衰。 直因言閣疏出司禮監黃賜、陳祖生意，為楊曄報復。 帝即斥賜、祖生於南京。 御史戴縉者，佞人也，九年秩滿不得遷。 窺帝旨，盛稱直功。 詔復開西廠，以千戶吳綬為鎮撫，直焰愈熾。 未幾，令東廠官校誣奏項忠，且諷言官郭鏜、馮貫等論忠違法事。 帝命三法司、錦衣衛會問。 眾知出直意，無敢違，竟勒忠為民。 而左都御史李賓亦失直旨褫職，大學士輅亦罷去。 一時九卿劾罷者，尚書董方、薛遠及侍郎滕昭、程萬里等數十人。 以所善王越為兵部尚書兼左都御史，陳鉞為右副都御史巡撫遼東。
In the fifth month, Grand Secretaries Shang Lu, Wan An, Liu Xu, and Liu Ji submitted a memorial reporting his crimes. The emperor was thunderstruck and ordered the Directorate of Ceremonial Service eunuchs Huai'en, Qin Ji, and Huang Gao to go to the Grand Secretariat, where they sternly delivered the imperial order and said: "Who suggested this memorial? Lu recited Zhi's crimes in full, then said: "We are of one mind and one purpose, removing harm for the state, with no thought of rank or order." Xu burst into tears as he spoke. Huai'en then reported the facts truthfully. After a while, the imperial order came back expressing consolation. The next day, memorials from Minister Zhong and the various grandees also came in. The emperor had no choice but to abolish the Western Depot, had Huai'en list Zhi's crimes and pardon him, ordered him back to the Imperial Horse Directorate, reassigned Wei Ying to a frontier guard, and scattered the various banner guards back to the Brocade Guard. Both court and commoners were overjoyed. Yet the emperor's favor toward Zhi did not decline. Zhi then said that the Grand Secretariat's memorial had been prompted by the Directorate of Ceremonial Service eunuchs Huang Ci and Chen Zusheng, as revenge for Yang Ye. The emperor immediately exiled Ci and Zusheng to Nanjing. The censor Dai Jin was a sycophant; when his nine-year term was up, he failed to get promoted. He read the emperor's intentions and loudly praised Zhi's merits. An edict reopened the Western Depot, with the thousand-household officer Wu Shou made commander; Zhi's arrogance burned even more fiercely. Soon he had the East Depot officials and guards falsely memorialize against Xiang Zhong, and also prompted the remonstrance officials Guo Tang, Feng Guan, and others to speak on Zhong's illegal conduct. The emperor ordered the three judicial offices and the Brocade Guard to meet and question him. Everyone knew it was Zhi's intention and no one dared oppose it, so they ultimately reduced Zhong to commoner status. The Left Grand Censor Li Bin also lost his office for offending Zhi's wishes, and Grand Secretary Lu was also dismissed. Among the many high ministers impeached and dismissed at that time were the ministers Dong Fang and Xue Yuan, as well as vice ministers Teng Zhao, Cheng Wanli, and dozens of others. He put his close ally Wang Yue in office as Minister of War and concurrently Left Grand Censor, and Chen Yue was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to serve as governor of Liaodong.
36
十五年秋，詔直巡邊，率飛騎日馳數百里，御史、主事等官迎拜馬首，箠撻守令。 各邊都御史畏直，服櫜迎謁，供張百里外。 至遼東，陳鉞郊迎蒲伏，廚傳尤盛，左右皆有賄。 直大悅。 惟河南巡撫秦纮與直抗禮，而密奏直巡邊擾民。 帝弗省。 兵部侍郎馬文升方撫諭遼東，直至不為禮，又輕鉞，被陷坐戍，由是直威勢傾天下。
In the autumn of the fifteenth year, an edict sent Zhi to inspect the border; he led fast cavalry and rode hundreds of li a day, while censors, section chiefs, and other officials came out to bow at his horse's head, and he flogged the border magistrates. The Grand Censors of the various borders feared Zhi, wore their armor and went out to greet him, and provided lavish hospitality more than a hundred li away. When he reached Liaodong, Chen Yue came out to greet him in the suburbs and lay prostrate before him; the kitchens and courier stations were especially lavish, and everyone around him accepted bribes. Zhi was greatly pleased. Only Qin Hong, the governor of Henan, stood on ceremony with Zhi, and secretly memorialized that Zhi's border inspection was disturbing the people. The emperor ignored it. When Vice Minister of War Ma Wensheng was pacifying Liaodong, Zhi arrived and did not treat him with courtesy, and he also slighted Yue; as a result, they were framed and sentenced to frontier garrison duty, and from then on Zhi's power and influence overshadowed the whole realm.

直年少喜兵。 陳鉞諷直征伏當加，立邊功自固。 直聽之，用撫寧侯朱永總兵，而自監其軍。 師還，永封保國公，鉞晉右都御史，直加祿米。 又用王越言，詐稱亦思馬因犯邊。 詔永同越西討，直為監軍。 越封威寧伯，直再加祿米。 已，伏當加寇遼東，亦思馬因寇大同，殺掠甚眾。 遼東巡按強珍發鉞奸狀，直右鉞謫珍。 於是惡直者，指王越、陳鉞為二鉞。 小中官阿醜工俳優，一日於帝前為醉者謾罵狀。 人言駕至，謾如故。 言汪太監至，則避走。 曰：「今人但知汪太監也。 」又為直狀，操兩鉞趨帝前。 旁人問之，曰：「吾將兵，仗此兩鉞耳。 」問何鉞，曰：「王越、陳鉞也。 」帝聽然而笑，稍稍悟，然廷臣猶未敢攻直也。 會東廠尚銘獲賊得厚賞，直忌，且怒銘不告。 銘懼，乃廉得其所泄禁中秘語奏之，盡發王越交通不法事，帝始疏直。
Zhi was young and loved military affairs. Chen Yue urged Zhi to campaign with Fudangjia, seeking to establish border merit and secure himself. Zhi accepted it, using Marquis of Funing Zhu Yong as the overall commander and supervising the army himself. When the army returned, Yong was enfeoffed as Duke of Baoguo, Yue was promoted to Right Grand Censor, and Zhi was given additional grain stipends. He also followed Wang Yue's suggestion and falsely claimed that Yisimayin had raided the border. An edict ordered Yong to campaign west together with Yue, with Zhi serving as supervising officer. Yue was enfeoffed as Marquis of Weining, and Zhi again received extra grain stipends. Afterward, Fudangjia raided Liaodong, and Yisimayin raided Datong, killing and plundering many people. The surveillance censor Qiang Zhen in Liaodong exposed Yue's criminal conduct, and Zhi sided with Yue and demoted Zhen. Thereupon those who hated Zhi referred to Wang Yue and Chen Yue as the two Yues. The junior eunuch Acho was skilled at comic performance; one day before the emperor he acted out the manner of a drunken man cursing. When someone said the carriage had arrived, he kept cursing as before. When it was said that the arrival was Wang the eunuch, he ran off to hide. He said: "Nowadays people only know Wang the eunuch." He also performed the role of Zhi, carrying two axes and striding before the emperor. When others asked him about it, he said: "I am a soldier; I rely on these two axes." When asked which axes, he said: "Wang Yue and Chen Yue." The emperor smiled knowingly, but the court ministers still did not dare attack Zhi. When the East Depot eunuch Shang Ming captured a bandit and received a rich reward, Zhi became jealous and also angry that Ming had not reported it. Ming was afraid, so he secretly learned what confidential palace words had been leaked and reported them, fully exposing Wang Yue's unlawful dealings, and only then did the emperor begin to distance himself from Zhi.

十七年秋，命直偕越往宣府禦敵。 敵退，直請班師。 不許，徙鎮大同，而盡召將吏還，獨留直、越。 直既久鎮不得還，寵日衰。 給事御史交章奏其苛擾，請仍罷西廠。 閣臣萬安亦力言之。 而大同巡撫郭鏜復言直與總兵許寧不和，恐誤邊事。 帝乃調直南京御馬監，罷西廠不復設。 中外欣然。 尋又以言官言，降直奉御，而褫逐其黨王越、戴縉、吳綬等。 陳鉞已致仕，不問。 韋瑛後坐他事誅，人皆快之，然直竟良死。 縉由御史不數年至南京工部尚書。 越、鉞頗以材進。 縉無他能，工側媚而已。
In the autumn of the seventeenth year, the emperor ordered Zhi to go with Yue to Xuanfu to resist the enemy. When the enemy retreated, Zhi requested that the army withdraw. This was not permitted; the garrison was moved to Datong, all the generals and officials were summoned back, and only Zhi and Yue were left. After Zhi had remained at the garrison for a long time without being allowed to return, his favor gradually declined. Assistant secretaries and censors jointly memorialized against his harsh disruption and requested that the Western Depot be abolished again. Grand Secretary Wan An also strongly argued for it. The governor of Datong, Guo Tang, also said that Zhi and the general commander Xu Ning were not on good terms and that this might harm border affairs. The emperor then transferred Zhi to the Nanjing Imperial Horse Directorate and abolished the Western Depot for good. Both court and commoners were delighted. Soon afterward, on the advice of the remonstrance officials, Zhi was reduced to a fengyu officer, and his allies Wang Yue, Dai Jin, Wu Shou, and others were stripped and dismissed. Chen Yue had already retired, so he was not investigated. Wei Ying was later executed for another offense, which everyone welcomed, though Zhi himself ultimately died a natural death. Jin, starting as a censor, became the Nanjing Minister of Works in only a few years. Yue and Yue had considerable ability and were promoted on merit. Jin had no special talent, only a knack for flattering and currying favor.

西廠廢，尚銘遂專東廠事。 聞京師有富室，輒以事羅織，得重賄乃已。 賣官鬻爵，無所不至。 帝尋覺之，謫充南京凈軍，籍其家，輦送內府，數日不盡。 而陳準代為東廠。 準素善懷恩，既代銘，誡諸校尉曰：「有大逆，告我。 非是，若勿預也。 」都人安之。
After the Western Depot was abolished, Shang Ming took sole charge of the East Depot. Whenever he heard of a wealthy family in the capital, he would frame them on some charge and stop only after extracting a heavy bribe. Selling offices and titles, he stopped at nothing. The emperor soon discovered it, demoted him to servile duty in Nanjing, confiscated his family, and had the goods carted into the inner palace, where even after several days they still had not been fully emptied. Chen Zhun then replaced him at the East Depot. Zhun had long been friendly with Huai'en; after taking Ming's place, he warned the sergeants: "If there is a grave rebellion, report it to me. If not, you need not concern yourselves with it." The people of the capital felt at ease.

梁芳者，憲宗朝內侍也。 貪黷諛佞，與韋興比。 而諂萬貴妃，日進美珠珍寶悅妃意。 其黨錢能、韋眷、王敬等，爭假采辦名，出監大鎮。 帝以妃故，不問也。 妖人李孜省、僧繼曉皆由芳進，共為奸利。 取中旨授官，累數千人，名傳奉官，有白衣躐至太常卿者。 陜西巡撫鄭時論芳被黜，陜民哭送之。 帝聞頗悔，斥傳奉官十人，系六人獄，詔自後傳旨授官者俱覆奏，然不罪芳也。 刑部員外郎林俊以劾芳及繼曉下獄。 久之，帝視內帑，見累朝金七窖俱盡，謂芳及韋興曰：「糜費帑藏，實由汝二人。 」興不敢對。 芳曰：「建顯靈宮及諸祠廟，為陛下祈萬年福耳。 」帝不懌曰：「吾不汝瑕，後之人將與汝計矣」。 芳大懼，遂說貴妃勸帝廢太子，而立興王。 會泰山累震，占者言應在東朝。 帝懼，乃止。 孝宗立，謫芳居南京，尋下獄，興亦斥退。 正德初，群閹復薦興司香太和山，兼分守湖廣行都司地方。 尚書劉大夏、給事中周璽、御史曹來旬諫，不聽。 興遂復用，而芳卒廢以死。
Liang Fang. Liang Fang was an inner attendant of the Chenghua Emperor's reign. He was greedy, rapacious, and flattering, and associated with Wei Xing. He also flattered Empress Wan, daily presenting fine pearls and jewels to please her. His followers Qian Neng, Wei Juan, Wang Jing, and others all rushed to borrow the name of purchasing supplies and go out to supervise major garrisons. Because of the empress, the emperor did not investigate them. The sorcerer Li Ziseng and the monk Jixiao were both introduced by Fang and joined in their profiteering. Using imperial instructions, they conferred office on several thousand men, known as transmission-offering officials, and even commoners leaped directly to the rank of Minister of Rites. When Zheng Shi, governor of Shaanxi, criticized Fang and was removed, the people of Shaanxi wept as they saw him off. The emperor heard of it and somewhat regretted it; he dismissed ten transmission-offering officials and jailed six others, and issued an edict that from then on all appointments made by imperial instruction had to be reviewed and reported, though Fang himself was not punished. When Assistant Minister Lin Jun of the Ministry of Justice impeached Fang and Jixiao, he was thrown into prison. After some time, when the emperor inspected the inner treasury and saw that the seven gold vaults of successive reigns were all emptied, he said to Fang and Wei Xing: "You two are truly the ones who have wasted the treasury. Xing did not dare answer. Fang said: "We built the Xianling Palace and the various shrines only to pray for Your Majesty's ten-thousand-year blessing. The emperor said unhappily: "I do not fault you now, but later people will settle accounts with you." Fang was deeply frightened and then persuaded the empress to urge the emperor to depose the crown prince and install the Prince of Xing instead. Then Mount Tai shook repeatedly, and the diviners said the omen pointed to the eastern palace. The emperor became afraid and stopped. When Xiaozong ascended the throne, Fang was demoted to residence in Nanjing, soon thrown into prison, and Xing was also dismissed. At the start of Zhengde, the eunuchs once again recommended Xing for the incense office at Mount Taihe and, in addition, for joint defense of the Huguang regional command area. Minister Liu Daxia, Assistant Secretary Zhou Xi, and Censor Cao Laixun remonstrated, but he would not listen. Xing was then again brought back into use, while Fang eventually was dismissed and died.
41
錢能，芳黨也。 憲宗時，鄭忠鎮貴州，韋朗鎮遼東，能鎮雲南，並恣縱，而能尤橫。 貴州巡撫陳宣劾忠，因請盡撤諸鎮監，帝不允。 而雲南巡按御史郭陽顧上疏譽能，請留之雲南。 舊制，安南貢道出廣西，後請改由雲南，弗許也。 能詐言安南捕盜兵入境，請遣指揮使郭景往諭其王，詔從之。 能遂令景以玉帶、彩繒、犬馬遺王，紿其貢使改道雲南。 邊吏格之不得入，乃去。 復遣景與指揮盧安等索寶貨於幹崖、孟密諸土司，至逼淫曩罕弄女孫，許為奏授宣撫。 逾三年，事發。 詔巡撫都御史王恕廉之，捕景，景赴井死。 再遣刑部郎中鍾蕃往按，事皆實。 帝宥能，而致其黨九人於法。 指揮姜和、李祥不就逮，能復上疏為二人求宥，帝曲從之。 巡按御史甄希賢復劾能杖守礦千戶一人死，亦不罪。 召歸，安置南京。 復夤緣得南京守備。 時恕為南京參贊尚書，能心憚恕不敢肆。 久之卒。
Qian Neng. Qian Neng was a follower of Fang. He was skilled at flattery and had no other merit. He first served in the inner palace; later he was promoted to eunuch of the Imperial Horse Directorate. When those with rank and favor entered the palace, he always stayed close and waited on them. Because he was good at flattering the empress, he was often favored. When his mother died, he was granted leave to return home for the funeral, and on the way back he passed by the Zi River. At the time there was drought; the people were all carrying water, while the corpses of those who had died along the road were strewn about in great numbers. He at once had a trench dug on the road and buried them all. The local people all praised him. By the middle of Chenghua he was in charge of the Imperial Horse Directorate. He took under his wing the imperial son-in-law Guo Chang and the Brocade Guard commander He Dian, and they were more intimate than brothers. Chang and Dian served him in cheating people, and the people's evil was unbearable. In the sixth month of the second year of Hongzhi, he was executed along with his family. His property was worth three hundred thousand, and he was notorious as one of the treacherous eunuchs of the age. Wei Jun. Wei Jun was a man of Fuzhou. He was selected into the inner school hall when still young. The emperor favored his nimble speech and sent him on missions to the four directions, all of which succeeded. He was promoted to eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service. When Minister of Personnel Wang Shu criticized Liang, Jun hated him.
42
韋眷、王敬亦芳黨。 眷為廣東市舶太監，縱賈人通諸番，聚珍寶甚富。 請以廣南均徭戶六十隸市舶。 布政使彭韶爭之，詔給其半。 眷又誣奏布政使陳選，被逮道卒，自是，人莫敢逆眷者。 弘治初，眷因結蔡用妄舉李父貴冒紀太后族，降左少監，撤回京。 事詳《紀太后傳》。
When Jun was running his schemes, he had Wang Bin, a minister from Handan, investigate and punish him, all because of an old grudge. Now that Liang had been dismissed, Jun could no longer conceal his behavior and was demoted to the Nanjing imperial wardrobe office. He also lost his power and eventually died in resentment. Wei Zhen. Wei Zhen was a man of Pingxiang. He entered the inner school hall as a youth. He was transferred to the Imperial Horse Directorate and served in the field garrisons of the capital. Because he was diligent and cautious, he was promoted to director of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service.

王敬好左道，信妖人王臣。 使南方，挾臣同行。 偽為詔，括書畫、古玩，聚白金十萬餘兩。 至蘇州，召諸生使錄妖書，且辱之。 諸生大嘩。 巡撫王恕以聞。 東廠尚銘亦發其事。 詔斬臣，而黜敬充孝陵衛凈軍。
He had little favor and was exiled to the sea-garrison offices in Nanjing. Then he was transferred back and repeatedly promoted until he became a eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service. The emperor ordered him to manage the Left Military Commission. He had relations with the Prince of Anhua and advised him to secure himself by maintaining readiness. The students were in great uproar. Governor Wang Shu reported it. The East Depot eunuch Shang Ming also exposed the matter. An edict ordered that the minister be executed, and Jing was demoted to the pure-duty eunuchs of the Xiaoling Guard.
