何鼎
He Ding
45
何鼎，餘杭人，一名文鼎，性忠直。 弘治初，為長隨，上疏請革傳奉官，為儕輩所忌。 壽寧侯張鶴齡兄弟出入宮禁，嘗侍內庭宴。 帝如廁，鶴齡倚酒戴帝冠，鼎心怒。 他日鶴齡復窺禦帷，鼎持大瓜欲擊之，奏言：「二張大不敬，無人臣禮。 」皇后激帝怒，下鼎錦衣獄。 問主使，鼎曰：「有。 」問為誰，曰：「孔子、孟子也。 」給事中龐泮、御史吳山及尚書周經、主事李昆、進士吳宗周先後論救，帝以後故，俱不納。 後竟使太監李廣杖殺鼎。 帝追思之，賜祭勒其文於碑。 是時，中官多守法，奉詔出鎮者，福建鄧原、浙江麥秀、河南藍忠、宣府劉清，皆謙潔愛民。 兵部上其事，賜敕旌勵。 又有司禮太監蕭敬者，歷事英宗、憲宗，諳習典故，善鼓琴。 帝嘗語劉大夏曰：「蕭敬朕所顧問，然未嘗假以權也。 」獨李廣、蔣琮得帝寵任，後二人俱敗，而敬至世宗朝，年九十餘始卒。
He Ding, also called Deng Yuan, was from Yuhang and was by nature loyal and straightforward. At the start of Hongzhi, as a lowly attendant, he submitted a memorial asking that transmission-offering officials be abolished, and was disliked by his peers for it. The brothers of Marquis of Shouning, Zhang Heling, came and went in the palace gates and once attended a banquet in the inner court. When the emperor went to the latrine, Heling, drunk, put on the emperor's crown, and Ding was furious in his heart. Another day Heling again peeped behind the imperial curtain, and Ding picked up a large melon to strike him; he then memorialized: "The two Zhang brothers are extremely disrespectful and show no ministerial propriety." The empress stirred the emperor's anger, and Ding was sent to the Brocade Guard prison. When asked who had instructed him, Ding said: "There was one." When asked who it was, he said: "Confucius and Mencius." Assistant secretary Pang Pan, censor Wu Shan, Minister Zhou Jing, chief clerk Li Kun, and the jinshi Wu Zongzhou all successively pleaded for his life, but because of the empress, the emperor would not accept any of it. In the end the emperor had the eunuch Li Guang beat Ding to death. Later the emperor remembered him, granted sacrificial rites, and had his text engraved on a stele. At that time many palace eunuchs kept the law; those sent out to garrison posts included Deng Yuan of Fujian, Mai Xiu of Zhejiang, Lan Zhong of Henan, and Liu Qing of Xuanfu, all of whom were modest, pure, and loving toward the people. The Ministry of War reported their conduct, and they were rewarded with an edict of commendation. There was also the Directorate of Ceremonial Service eunuch Xiao Jing, who served the Yingzong and Xianzong emperors through many years, knew the precedents well, and was skilled at playing the qin. The emperor once told Liu Daxia: "Xiao Jing is the one I consult with, but I have never given him power." Only Li Guang and Jiang Cong won the emperor's favor and trust; later both men fell, while Jing lived on into the time of the Jiajing Emperor and only died at more than ninety years of age.
46
李廣，孝宗時太監也。 以符箓禱祀蠱帝，因為奸弊，矯旨授傳奉官，如成化間故事，四方爭納賄賂。 又擅奪畿內民田，專鹽利巨萬。 起大第，引玉泉山水，前後繞之。 給事葉紳、御史張縉等交章論劾，帝不問。 十一年，廣勸帝建毓秀亭於萬歲山。 亭成，幼公主殤，未幾，清寧宮災。 日者言廣建亭犯歲忌，太皇太后恚曰：「今日李廣，明日李廣，果然禍及矣。 」廣懼自殺。 帝疑廣有異書，使使即其家索之，得賂籍以進，多文武大臣名，饋黃白米各千百石。 帝驚曰：「廣食幾何，乃受米如許。 」左右曰：「隱語耳，黃者金，白者銀也。 」帝怒，下法司究治。 諸交結廣者，走壽寧侯張鶴齡求解，乃寢勿治。 廣初死時，司設監太監為請祠額葬祭，及是以大學士劉健等言，罷給祠額，猶賜祭。
Li Guang. Li Guang was an eunuch of the Xiaozong reign. He used talismans and prayers to bewitch the emperor, then engaged in fraud and corruption, forged edicts to appoint transmission-offering officials as in the Chenghua era, and people from all quarters rushed to bribe him. He also seized commoner lands within the capital region and monopolized the salt profits to a vast degree. He built a great mansion and drew water from Jade Spring Hill to surround it on every side. Assistant secretary Ye Shen and censor Zhang Jin and others repeatedly memorialized against him, but the emperor did not question it. In the eleventh year, Guang urged the emperor to build Yuxiu Pavilion on Longevity Hill. When the pavilion was finished, a young princess died, and not long after the Qingning Palace caught fire. The astrologers said Guang's building of the pavilion violated the year taboo. The Grand Empress Dowager angrily said: "Today Li Guang, tomorrow Li Guang - sure enough, disaster has come of it." Guang, afraid, killed himself. The emperor suspected Guang had secret writings and sent envoys to search his house, where they found a register of bribes to be presented, with many names of civil and military ministers, and gifts of yellow and white rice in quantities of hundreds of shi each. The emperor was shocked and said: "How much can Guang eat, that he would receive so much rice?" Those around him said: "It is coded language; the yellow stands for gold and the white stands for silver." The emperor was angered and sent the case to the judicial offices for investigation and punishment. Those who had associated with Guang went to Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling to ask for help, and then the matter was put aside and not pursued. When Guang first died, the eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service had requested a shrine plaque and funeral rites; at this point, on the advice of Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others, the grant of a shrine plaque was canceled, though sacrificial rites were still bestowed.
47
蔣琮，大興人。 孝宗時，守備南京。 沿江蘆場，舊隸三廠。 成化初，江浦縣田多沈於江，而瀕江生沙洲六，民請耕之，以補沈江田額。 洲與蘆場近，又瓦屑壩廢地及石城門外湖地，故不隸三廠。 太監黃賜為守備時，受奸民獻，俱指為蘆場，盡收其利。 民已失業，而歲額租課仍責償之民。 孝宗立，縣民相率醞於朝，下南京御史姜綰等覆按。 弘治二年，綰等劾琮與民爭利，且用揭帖抗詔旨。 琮條辨綰疏，而泛及御史劉愷、方嶽等及南京諸司違法事。 給事中韓重因星變請斥琮及太監郭鏞等，以弭天怒，未報。 而太監陳祖生復奏戶部主事盧錦、給事中方向私種南京後湖田事。 後湖者，洪武時置黃冊庫其中，令主事、給事中各一人守之，百司不得至。 歲久湖塞，錦、向於湖灘稍種蔬伐葦，給公用，故為祖生所奏。 事下南京法司。 適郭鏞奉使兩廣，道南京，往觀焉。 御史纮等因劾鏞擅遊禁地。 鏞怒，歸醞於帝，言府尹楊守隨勘錦、向失出，御史不劾奏，獨繩內臣。 帝乃遣太監何穆、大理寺少卿楊謐再勘後湖田，並覆綰、琮訐奏事。
Jiang Cong. Jiang Cong was a native of Daxing. During the Xiaozong reign, he served in the Nanjing garrison. The reed fields along the river had formerly belonged to the three depots. At the beginning of Chenghua, much of the land in Jiangpu County had sunk into the river, and six sandbars had formed along the bank; the people asked to farm them in order to make up for the lost riverland quota. The sandbars were near the reed fields, and so were the wasteland of Waxie Dam and the lake land outside Shicheng Gate; therefore they were not placed under the three depots. When the eunuch Huang Ci served as garrison supervisor, he accepted what wicked locals offered and called all of it reed fields, taking all the profits for himself. The people had already lost their livelihood, yet the annual rent and levies were still demanded from them. When Xiaozong ascended the throne, the county people went to court in a group, and the Nanjing censors Jiang Wan and others were sent to re-examine the matter. In the second year of Hongzhi, Wan and the others impeached Cong for competing with the people for profit and for using a memorial slip to oppose the imperial edict. Cong itemized his rebuttal to Wan's memorial and broadly implicated censor Liu Kai, Fang Yue, and the illegal conduct of the various Nanjing offices. Assistant secretary Han Zhong, because of an eclipse, asked that Cong and eunuch Guo Yong be removed to avert Heaven's anger, but no reply was given. Then eunuch Chen Zusheng also reported that Ministry of Revenue chief clerk Lu Jin and assistant secretary Fang Yang had privately planted crops on the Nanjing Houhu Lake land. Houhu Lake had held the Yellow Register repository since Hongwu's time; one chief clerk and one assistant secretary were assigned to guard it, and the hundred offices were forbidden to approach it. Over the years the lake had silted up; Jin and Xiang had planted vegetables and cut reeds on the lake shore for public use, and so Zusheng reported them. The case was sent to the Nanjing judicial offices. At that moment Guo Yong, on a mission to the two Guang regions, passed through Nanjing and went to see it. The censors and others therefore impeached Yong for unlawfully entering a forbidden place for amusement. Yong was angry and, on returning, reported to the emperor that prefectural administrator Yang Shunsui had examined Jin and Xiang's case improperly, that the censors had failed to impeach and report it, and that only the inner officials had been disciplined. The emperor then sent eunuch He Mu and Vice Minister of the Court of Judicature Yang Mi to re-examine the Houhu Lake land case and also to review the memorials accusing Wan and Cong.
48
明年，奏上，褫錦職，謫守隨、向以下官有差。 又勘琮不當受獻地，私囑勘官，所訐事皆誣，綰等劾琮亦多不實，並宜逮治。 詔逮綰等。 御史伊宏、給事中陳矞等皆言不宜以一內臣而置御史十人於獄，不聽。 綰等鐫級調外，而宥琮不問。 時劉吉竊柄，素惡南京御史劾己，故興此獄。 尚書王恕、李敏，給事中趙竑，御史張賓先後言琮、綰同罪異罰，失平，亦不納。 琮由是益無忌。 久之，廣洋衛指揮石文通奏琮僭侈殺人，掘聚寶山傷皇陵氣，及毆殺商人諸罪。 琮竟免死，充孝陵凈軍。
The next year the report was submitted; Jin was stripped of office, and Shunsui, Xiang, and the others were demoted by various degrees. It was also determined that Cong should not have accepted the donated land, that he had privately instructed the investigators, that all the accusations he made were false, and that the memorials against Cong by Wan and the others were likewise mostly untrue; they should all be arrested and investigated. An edict ordered that Wan and the others be arrested. The censors Yi Hong and assistant secretary Chen Yu and others all said that it was improper to imprison ten censors because of one inner servant, but the emperor would not listen. Wan and the others were demoted and sent out, while Cong was pardoned and left unpunished. At the time Liu Ji secretly held power, and because he had long hated the Nanjing censors for impeaching him, he stirred up this case. Minister Wang Shu, Li Min, assistant secretary Zhao Hong, and censor Zhang Bin successively said that Cong and Wan should receive the same punishment and that the unequal penalties were unjust, but the emperor still would not accept it. From this point on Cong became even more unrestrained. After some time, Shi Wentong, commander of the Guangyang Guard, memorialized that Cong was extravagant and cruel, that he had killed people, dug into Mount Jubao and injured the imperial tomb's vital energy, and beaten and killed merchants and others. In the end Cong escaped death and was assigned to be a pure-duty eunuch at Xiaoling Tomb.
49
劉瑾，興平人。 本談氏子，依中官劉姓者以進，冒其姓。 孝宗時，坐法當死，得免。 已，得侍武宗東宮。 武宗即位，掌鐘鼓司，與馬永成、高鳳、羅祥、魏彬、丘聚、谷大用、張永並以舊恩得幸，人號「八虎」，而瑾尤狡狠。 嘗慕王振之為人，日進鷹犬、歌舞、角之戲，導帝微行。 帝大歡樂之，漸信用瑾，進內官監，總督團營。 孝宗遺詔罷中官監槍及各城門監局，瑾皆格不行，而勸帝令內臣鎮守者各貢萬金。 又奏置皇莊，漸增至三百餘所，畿內大擾。
Liu Jin. Liu Jin was a man of Xingping. He was originally the son of the Tan family; he entered office by relying on an inner official surnamed Liu and took that surname himself. During the Xiaozong reign he was convicted under the law and should have died, but escaped. Afterward he was able to serve the future Emperor Wuzong in the eastern palace. When Wuzong ascended the throne, he took charge of the Clock and Drum Bureau. With Ma Yongcheng, Gao Feng, Luo Xiang, Wei Bin, Qiu Ju, Gu Dayong, and Zhang Yong, all favored through old ties, he was one of the so-called Eight Tigers, and Jin in particular was sly and ruthless. He used to admire the way Wang Zhen behaved, and every day he introduced hawks, dogs, singing, dancing, and wrestling to lead the emperor into secret outings. The emperor was greatly delighted by it, gradually trusted Jin, promoted him to the Inner Office Directorate, and put him in overall command of the group armies. He also had close dealings with Prince of Anhua Zhu Chenhao and often secretly sent letters to him. Jin even had a memorial gate built in the palace road and a shrine erected to himself, and privately assumed the authority of the eight offices.
50
外廷知八人誘帝遊宴，大學士劉健、謝遷、李東陽驟諫，不聽。 尚書張升，給事中陶諧、胡煜、楊一瑛、張襘，御史王渙、趙佑，南京給事御史李光翰、陸昆等，交章論諫，亦不聽。 五官監候楊源以星變陳言，帝意頗動。 健、遷等復連疏請誅瑾，戶部尚書韓文率諸大臣繼之。 帝不得已，使司禮太監陳寬、李榮、王嶽至閣，議遣瑾等居南京。 三反，健等執不可。 尚書許進曰：「過激將有變。 」健不從。 王嶽者，素謇直，與太監範亨、徐智心嫉八人，具以健等語告帝，且言閣臣議是。 健等方約文及諸九卿詰朝伏闕面爭，而吏部尚書焦芳馳白瑾。 瑾大懼，夜率永成等伏帝前環泣。 帝心動，瑾因曰：「害奴等者王嶽。 嶽結閣臣欲制上出入，故先去所忌耳。 且鷹犬何損萬幾。 若司禮監得人，左班官安敢如是。 」帝大怒，立命瑾掌司禮監，永成掌東廠，大用掌西廠，而夜收嶽及亨、智充南京凈軍。 旦日諸臣入朝，將伏闕，知事已變，於是健、東陽皆求去。 帝獨留東陽，而令焦芳入閣，追殺嶽、亨於途，箠智折臂。 時正德元年十月也。
He sent spies all over the country to secretly gather information on ministers and the people. He also often spoke of Chuanyong, the man who had been used by Wang Zhen, and claimed that Zhen's old example was not enough to compare with him. Yang Yuan, a registrar of the Five Offices, memorialized on account of a celestial anomaly, and the emperor was somewhat moved. Jian and Qian and the others again sent repeated memorials calling for Jin's execution, and Han Wen, the Minister of Revenue, led the rest of the ministers in pressing the same request. The emperor had no choice, so he sent the eunuchs Chen Kuan, Li Rong, and Wang Yue of the Directorate of Ceremonial to the Grand Secretariat to discuss sending Jin and the others to live in Nanjing. After three rounds of rejection, Jian and the others still insisted that it could not be done. Minister Xu Jin warned, 'If you push this too hard, there will be trouble.' Jian refused to yield. Wang Yue had always been straightforward and upright. Together with the eunuchs Fan Heng and Xu Zhi, all of whom hated the eight men, he reported Jian and the others' words to the emperor in full and said the Grand Secretariat had agreed. Jian and the others were just arranging with Han Wen and the other Nine Ministers to kneel at the palace gate at dawn and confront him in person, when the Minister of Personnel Jiao Fang hurried to report to Jin. Jin was terrified, and that night he led Yongcheng and the others to kneel before the emperor and cry around him. The emperor was moved, and Jin then said, 'The one harming your slaves is Wang Yue.' Yue had aligned himself with the Grand Secretariat and wanted to control the emperor's movements, so he was first trying to remove those he disliked. Besides, how could mere hawks and hounds harm the great affairs of state? If the Directorate of Ceremonial had the right man, how would the officials on the left dare act like this? The emperor was enraged and at once ordered Jin to head the Directorate of Ceremonial, Yongcheng to head the Eastern Depot, and Dayong to head the Western Depot, and that night had Yue and Heng and Zhi arrested and consigned to the Nanjing eunuch corps. The next day the ministers came to court intending to kneel at the palace gate, but when they learned the situation had changed, Jian and Dongyang both asked to leave office. The emperor kept Dongyang alone, and ordered Jiao Fang into the Grand Secretariat, while men were sent after Yue and Heng and killed them on the road, and Zhi was beaten until his arm broke. This was the tenth month of Zhengde's first year.
51
瑾既得志，遂以事革韓文職，而杖責請留健、遷者給事中呂翀、劉郤及南京給事中戴銑等六人，御史薄彥徽等十五人。 守備南京武靖伯趙承慶、府尹陸珩、尚書林瀚，皆以傳翀、郤疏得罪，珩、瀚勒致仕，削承慶半祿。 南京副都御史陳壽，御史陳琳、王良臣，主事王守仁，復以救銑等謫杖有差。 瑾勢日益張，毛舉官僚細過，散布校尉，遠近偵伺，使人救過不贍。 因顓擅威福，悉遣黨閹分鎮各邊。 敘大同功，遷擢官校至一千五百六十餘人，又傳旨授錦衣官數百員。 《通鑒纂要》成，瑾誣諸翰林纂修官謄寫不謹，皆被譴，而命文華殿書辦官張駿等改謄，超拜官秩。 駿由光祿卿擢禮部尚書，他授京卿者數人，裝潢匠役悉授官。 創用枷法，給事中吉時，御史王時中，郎中劉繹、張瑋，尚寶卿顧璿，副使姚祥，參議吳廷舉等，並摭小過，枷瀕死，始釋而戍之。 其餘枷死者無數。 錦衣獄徽纆相屬。 惡錦衣僉事牟斌善視獄囚，杖而錮之。 府丞周璽、五官監候楊源杖至死。 源初以皇變陳言，罪瑾者也。 瑾每奏事，必偵帝為戲弄時。 帝厭之。 亟麾去曰：「吾用若何事，乃混我！ 」自此遂專決，不復白。
Once Jin had his way, he used the matter to remove Han Wen from office and beat the six men who had petitioned to keep Jian and Qian, including the giving-attendance officials Lü Chong and Liu Que and the Nanjing giving-attendance officials Dai Xian and the others, as well as fifteen censors such as Bo Yanhui. The Nanjing garrison commander, Earl of Wujing Zhao Chengqing, the prefect Lu Heng, and Minister Lin Han were all implicated because of memorials by Chong and Que; Heng and Han were forced to retire, and Chengqing's stipend was cut in half. The deputy Censor-in-chief Chen Shou of Nanjing, the censors Chen Lin and Wang Liangchen, and the principal secretary Wang Shouren were again punished by beating and demotion in varying degrees for having tried to save Xian and the others. Jin's power grew stronger by the day. He picked out the smallest faults in officials, spread his junior guards out to spy near and far, and made it impossible for people to repair their own mistakes. He thus monopolized power and favor and sent all his eunuch followers to be stationed at the various frontiers. For his achievements at Datong, more than 1,560 officers and guards were promoted, and an imperial order also appointed several hundred Brocade Guard officers. When the Compendium of Governance was completed, Jin falsely accused the Hanlin compilation officers of careless copying, and they were all reprimanded, while the palace copyist Zhang Jun and others were ordered to recopy it and were promoted far beyond their rank. Zhang Jun was promoted from Guanglu Minister to Minister of Rites; several others who had been given the rank of metropolitan minister were also elevated, and the craftsmen and attendants who did the finishing work were all granted office. He introduced the cangue punishment. Assistant secretary Ji Shi, censor Wang Shizhong, the langzhong Liu Yi and Zhang Wei, Shangbao minister Gu Xuan, vice commissioner Yao Xiang, and councilor Wu Tingju were all seized for small offenses, cangued nearly to death, and only then released and sent to frontier service. Countless others died under the cangue. The Brocade Guard prisons were packed with shackles and cords. Because he disliked Brocade Guard assistant commissioner Mou Bin for treating prisoners well, he had him beaten and confined. The prefectural vice magistrate Zhou Xi and the Five Offices registrar Yang Yuan were beaten to death. Yang had initially made a memorial speaking out on behalf of the changes in the emperor's horoscope, and he was one of those who had been guilty of Jin's crimes. Whenever Jin reported matters to the emperor, he had to first find out when the emperor was joking. The emperor grew tired of him. He quickly waved him away, saying: "I use you for what purpose, and yet you muddle me!" From then on he made the decisions himself and no longer reported them to others.
52
二年三月，瑾召群臣跪金水橋南，宣示奸黨，大臣則大學士劉健、謝遷，尚書則韓文、楊守隨、張敷華、林瀚，部曹則郎中李夢陽，主事王守仁、王綸、孫磐、黃昭，詞臣則檢討劉瑞，言路則給事中湯禮敬、陳霆、徐昂、陶諧、劉郤、艾洪、呂翀、任惠、李光翰、戴銑、徐蕃、牧相、徐暹、張良弼、葛嵩、趙士賢，御史陳琳、貢安甫、史良佐、曹閔、王弘、任諾、李熙、王蕃、葛浩、陸昆、張鳴鳳、蕭乾元、姚學禮、黃昭道、蔣欽、薄彥徽、潘鏜、王良臣、趙佑、何天衢、徐玨、楊璋、熊卓、朱廷聲、劉玉等，皆海內號忠直者也。 又令六科寅入酉出，使不得息，以困苦之。 令文臣毋輒予封誥，痛繩文吏。 寧王宸濠圖不軌，賂瑾求復護衛，瑾予之，濠反謀遂成。 瑾不學，每批答章奏，皆持歸私第，與妹婿禮部司務孫聰、華亭大猾張文冕相參決，辭率鄙冗，焦芳為潤色之，東陽頫首而已。
In the third month of the second year, Jin summoned the ministers to kneel south of the Jinshui Bridge and announced the treacherous faction: the grand secretaries Liu Jian and Xie Qian; the ministers Han Wen, Yang Shunsui, Zhang Fuhua, and Lin Han; the ministry officials, including the langzhong Li Mengyang and the chief clerks Wang Shouren, Wang Lun, Sun Pan, Huang Zhao, and others; the literary officials, including the compiler Liu Rui; the remonstrance officials, including assistant secretaries Tang Lijing, Chen Ting, Xu Ang, Tao Xie, Liu Qie, Ai Hong, Lü Chong, Ren Hui, Li Guanghan, Dai Xian, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Xu Xian, Zhang Liangbi, Ge Song, and Zhao Shixian; and the censors Chen Lin, Gong Anfu, Shi Liangzuo, Cao Min, Wang Hong, Ren Nuo, Li Xi, Wang Fan, Ge Hao, Lu Kun, Zhang Mingfeng, Xiao Qianyuan, Yao Xueli, Huang Zhaodao, Jiang Qin, Bo Yanhui, Pan Tang, Wang Liangchen, Zhao You, He Tianqu, Xu Jue, Yang Zhang, Xiong Zhuo, Zhu Tingsheng, Liu Yu, and others, all of whom were known throughout the empire as loyal and upright men. He also ordered the Six Departments to enter at the hour of yin and leave at the hour of you, denying them rest and wearing them down. He ordered that civil officials were not to be granted seals and patents at random, and he harshly restrained the clerks. When Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao plotted rebellion, he bribed Jin and asked to have his guards restored; Jin granted it, and Chenhao's later revolt was then fully set in motion. Jin was unlearned; whenever he annotated memorials and reports, he carried them back to his private residence and discussed them with his brother-in-law Sun Cong, a clerk in the Ministry of Rites, and with Zhang Wenmian, a great rogue of Huating. His language was crude and clumsy, so Jiao Fang polished it, and Dongyang could only bow his head and submit.
53
當是時，瑾權擅天下，威福任情。 有罪人溺水死，乃坐御史匡翼之罪。 嘗求學士吳儼賄，不得，又聽都御史劉宇讒，怒御史楊南金，乃以大計外吏奏中，落二人職。 授播州土司楊斌為四川按察使。 令奴婿閭潔督山東學政。 公侯勛戚以下，莫敢鈞禮，每私謁，相率跪拜。 章奏先具紅揭投瑾，號紅本，然後上通政司，號白本，皆稱劉太監而不名。 都察院奏讞誤名瑾，瑾怒詈之，都御史屠滽率屬跪謝乃已。 遣使察核邊倉，都御史周南、張鼐、馬中錫、湯全、劉憲，布政以下官孫祿、冒政、方矩、華福、金獻民、劉遜、郭緒、張翼，郎中劉繹、王藎等，並以赦前罪，下獄追補邊粟，憲至瘐死。 又察鹽課，杖巡鹽御史王潤，逮前運使寧舉、楊奇等。 察內甲字庫，謫尚書王佐以下百七十三人。 復創罰米法，嘗忤瑾者，皆擿發輸邊。 故尚書雍泰、馬文升、劉大夏、韓文、許進，都御史楊一清、李進、王忠，侍郎張縉，給事中趙士賢，任良弼，御史張津，陳順、喬恕、聶賢、曹來旬等數十人悉破家，死者繫其妻孥。
At that time Jin held power over the whole realm and dispensed favor and punishment as he wished. When a criminal drowned and died, the blame was placed on the censor Kuang Yizhi. He once sought a bribe from the scholar Wu Yan and got none; then, listening to the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he became angry with the censor Yang Nanjin and used the annual evaluation of outside officials to have the two of them removed from office. He appointed Yang Bin, a native chief of Bozhou, as Sichuan surveillance commissioner. He ordered his son-in-law Lü Jie to supervise the school administration of Shandong. Dukes, marquises, meritorious officers, and relatives by marriage all dared not insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they all knelt and bowed in turn. Memorials had first to be prepared as red slips and submitted to Jin, known as the red memorials; only then were they sent on to the Court of State Affairs as white memorials. In all cases he was called Eunuch Liu and not by name. When the Censorate referred to Jin by name in a judgment report, Jin cursed them in anger, and Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he stopped. He sent envoys to inspect the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with the provincial officials Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and the ministry officials Liu Yi, Wang Jin, and others, were all imprisoned for crimes supposedly covered by amnesty and made to repay border grain; Xian died in prison of illness. He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged the salt-surveillance censor Wang Run, and arrested the former transport commissioners Ning Ju and Yang Qi and others. He inspected the Inner Armor Character Treasury and demoted 173 people, including Minister Wang Zuo. He also invented the penalty of grain fines again; anyone who had offended Jin was all exposed and sent to the frontier. Thus ministers such as Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Ministers Zhang Jin; Assistant Secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens of others all lost their homes, and those who died left their wives and children bound up with them.
54
其年夏，御道有匿名書詆瑾所行事，瑾矯旨召百官跪奉天門下。 瑾立門左詰責，日暮收五品以下官盡下獄。 明日，大學士李東陽申救，瑾亦微聞此書乃內臣所為，始釋諸臣。 而主事何釴、順天推官周臣、進士陸伸已暍死。 是日酷暑，太監李榮以冰瓜啖群臣，瑾惡之。 太監黃偉憤甚，謂諸臣曰：「書所言皆為國為民事，挺身自承，雖死不失為好男子，奈何枉累他人。 」瑾怒，即日勒榮閑住，而逐偉南京。 時東廠、西廠緝事人四出，道路惶懼。 瑾復立內行廠，尤酷烈，中人以微法，無得全者。 又悉逐京師客傭，令寡婦盡嫁，喪不葬者焚之，輦下洶洶幾致亂。 都給事中許天錫欲劾瑾，懼弗克，懷疏自縊。
That summer, an anonymous letter was found on the imperial road attacking Jin's conduct, and Jin forged an edict summoning all the officials to kneel below Fengtian Gate. Jin stood at the left side of the gate and interrogated them; by evening he had all the officials of fifth rank and below taken into prison. The next day Grand Secretary Li Dongyang spoke up in their defense, and Jin also heard faintly that the letter had been written by inner officials, so he finally released the ministers. But the chief clerk He Yi, the magistrate of Shuntian, Zhou Chen, and the jinshi Lu Shen had already died of heatstroke. That day was oppressively hot; the eunuch Li Rong offered iced melons to the ministers, and Jin disliked it. The eunuch Huang Wei was furious and said to the ministers: "What the letter says is all for the state and the people. To step forward and take responsibility, even if one dies, is still the conduct of a good man. How can you falsely implicate others?" Jin was enraged, immediately ordered Rong to stand aside, and banished Wei to Nanjing. At that time the investigators of the East and West Depots were spread everywhere, and the roads were filled with fear. Jin also established an Internal Operating Depot, even more cruel and fierce; anyone who was caught by a minor offense was never let go whole. He also expelled all hired laborers from the capital, ordered all widows to remarry, and burned the bodies of those whose burials had not been completed; the capital seethed and nearly fell into disorder. The chief secretary of the capital administration, Xu Tianxi, wanted to impeach Jin but feared he would fail, so he kept the memorial with him and hanged himself.
55
瑾故急賄，凡入覲、出使官皆有厚獻。 給事中周鑰勘事歸，以無金自殺。 其黨張綵曰：「今天下所饋遺公者，非必皆私財，往往貸京師，而歸則以庫金償。 公奈何斂怨貽患。 」瑾然之。 會御史歐陽雲等十餘人以故事入賂，瑾皆舉發致罪。 乃遣給事、御史十四人分道盤察，有司爭厚斂以補帑。 所遣人率阿瑾意，專務搏擊，劾尚書顧佐、侶鐘、韓文以下數十人。 浙江鹽運使楊奇逋課死，至鬻其女孫。 而給事中安奎、潘希曾，御史趙時中、阮吉、張彧、劉子厲，以無重劾下獄。 奎、彧枷且死，李東陽疏救，始釋為民。 希曾等亦皆杖斥，忤意者謫斥有差。 又矯旨籍故都御史錢鉞、禮部侍郎黃景、尚書秦纮家。 凡瑾所逮捕，一家犯，鄰里皆坐，或瞰河居者，以河外居民坐之。 屢起大獄，冤號遍道路。 《孝宗實錄》成，翰林預纂修者當遷秩，瑾惡翰林官素不下己，調侍講吳一鵬等十六人南京六部。
Jin was especially eager for bribes; all officials who came to pay respects at court or were sent on missions had to make lavish offerings. Assistant secretary Zhou Yao returned from investigating a case and killed himself because he had no money. His faction Zhang Cai said: "These gifts brought to you from across the realm are not necessarily all personal funds; often they are borrowed in the capital and repaid with treasury money on the return trip." Why bring hatred on yourself and breed trouble? Jin agreed with him. When censors Ouyang Yun and more than ten others entered with bribes as usual, Jin exposed them all and brought them to punishment. He then sent fourteen assistant secretaries and censors out along different routes to inspect and seize, and the officials there all competed in heavy exactions to make up the treasury. The men he sent all catered to Jin's wishes and focused on striking at others; they impeached ministers such as Gu Zuo, Lü Zhong, and Han Wen and dozens more. The Zhejiang salt transport commissioner Yang Qi fell into arrears on the quota and died, and even his daughter and granddaughter were sold off. Assistant secretaries An Kui and Pan Xizeng, and censors Zhao Shizhong, Ruan Ji, Zhang Yu, and Liu Zili, were all imprisoned for not making a heavy enough accusation. Kui and Yu were cangued until they nearly died; only after Li Dongyang memorialized in their defense were they released to commoner status. Pan Xizeng and the others were also beaten and dismissed, and those who offended Jin's wishes were demoted in various degrees. He also forged an edict to confiscate the homes of former Grand Censor Qian Yue, Minister of Rites Huang Jing, and Minister Qin Hong. Anyone Jin seized was treated as guilty together with his neighbors if one household offended; if someone lived by the river bank, he was counted together with those living beyond the river. He repeatedly stirred up major cases, and cries of injustice filled the roads. When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong were completed, the Hanlin editors who had taken part were supposed to be promoted, but Jin disliked the Hanlin officials for always looking down on him, so he transferred sixteen men including lecturer Wu Yipeng to the Nanjing ministries.
56
是時，內閣焦芳、劉宇，吏部尚書張綵，兵部尚書曹元，錦衣衛指揮楊玉、石文義，皆為瑾腹心。 變更舊制，令天下巡撫入京受敕，輸瑾賂。 延綏巡撫劉宇不至，逮下獄。 宣府巡撫陸完後至，幾得罪，既賂，乃令試職視事。 都指揮以下求遷者，瑾第書片紙曰「某授某官」，兵部即奉行，不敢復奏。 邊將失律，賂入，即不問，有反升擢者。 又遣其黨丈邊塞屯地，誅求苛刻。 邊軍不堪，焚公廨，守臣諭之始定。 給事中高淓丈滄州，所劾治六十一人，至劾其父高銓以媚瑾。 又以謝遷故，令餘姚人毋授京官。 以占城國使人亞劉謀逆獄，裁江西鄉試額五十名，仍禁授京秩如餘姚，以焦芳惡彭華故也。 瑾又自增陜西鄉試額至百名，亦為芳增河南額至九十五名，以優其鄉士。 其年，帝大赦，瑾峻刑自如。 刑部尚書劉璟無所彈劾，瑾詬之。 璟懼，劾其屬王尚賓等三人，乃喜。 給事中郗夔核榆林功，懼失瑾意，自縊死。 給事中屈銓、祭酒王雲鳳請編瑾行事，著為律令。
At that time Grand Secretariat members Jiao Fang and Liu Yu, Minister of Personnel Zhang Cai, Minister of War Cao Yuan, and Brocade Guard commanders Yang Yu and Shi Wenyin were all Jin's trusted intimates. He changed the old system and made all provincial governors come to the capital to receive edicts and hand over bribes to Jin. Liu Yu, governor of Yansui, failed to appear and was arrested and imprisoned. Lu Wan, governor of Xuanfu, arrived later and nearly incurred punishment; after bribing them, he was allowed to take office and act in his post. When guard commanders and those below sought promotion, Jin would merely write a note saying, 'So-and-so is granted such-and-such office,' and the Ministry of War would carry it out without daring to report again. If border generals failed in discipline but paid bribes, nothing would be done; some were even promoted. He also sent his faction to measure the frontier garrisons and camps, demanding and extorting with extreme harshness. The frontier troops could not endure it, burned the government offices, and only calmed down after the local commanders persuaded them. Assistant secretary Gao Feng measured Cangzhou, and among the sixty-one people he impeached, he even impeached his own father Gao Quan to curry favor with Jin. Because of Xie Qian, he ordered that people from Yuyao were not to be appointed to court offices. In the case of the rebellion involving the Champa envoy A Liu Mou, he cut the quota for the Jiangxi provincial examination by fifty names and still forbade appointment to court office just as he had for Yuyao; this was because Jiao Fang hated Peng Hua. Jin also raised the Shaanxi provincial examination quota to one hundred, and likewise had Fang increase the Henan quota to ninety-five, to favor men from his own region. That year the emperor issued a general amnesty, but Jin continued his harsh punishments as before. Minister of Justice Liu Jing failed to find anything to impeach, and Jin cursed him for it. Liu Jing was frightened and impeached three of Jin's subordinates, Wang Shangbin and others, and Jin was pleased. Assistant secretary Xi Kui, while examining the merits at Yulin, feared losing Jin's favor and hanged himself. Assistant secretary Qu Quan and Grand Academy rector Wang Yunfeng asked that Jin's conduct be compiled and made into law.
57
五年四月，安化王寘鐇反，檄數瑾罪。 瑾始懼，匿其檄，而起都御史楊一清、太監張永為總督，討之。 初，與瑾同為八虎者，當瑾專政時，有所請多不應，永成、大用等皆怨瑾。 又欲逐永，永以譎免。 及永出師還，欲因誅瑾，一清為畫策，永意遂決。 瑾好招致術士，有俞日明者，妄言瑾從孫二漢當大貴。 兵仗局太監孫和數遺以甲仗，兩廣鎮監潘午、蔡昭又為造弓弩，瑾皆藏於家。 永捷疏至，將以八月十五日獻俘，瑾使緩其期。 永慮有變，遂先期入，獻俘畢，帝置酒勞永，瑾等皆侍。 及夜，瑾退，永出寘鐇檄，因奏瑾不法十七事。 帝已被酒，俯首曰：「瑾負我。 」永曰：「此不可緩。 」永成等亦助之。 遂執瑾，繫於菜廠，分遣官校封其內外私第。 次日晏朝後，帝出永奏示內閣，降瑾奉御，謫居鳳陽。 帝親籍其家，得偽璽一，穿宮牌五百及衣甲、弓弩、袞衣、玉帶諸違禁物。 又所常持扇，內藏利匕首二。 始大怒曰：「奴果反。 」趣付獄。 獄具，詔磔於市，梟其首，榜獄詞處決圖示天下。 族人、逆黨皆伏誅。 張綵獄斃，磔其屍。 閣臣焦芳、劉宇、曹元而下，尚書畢亨、朱恩等，共六十餘人，皆降謫。 已，廷臣奏瑾所變法，吏部二十四事，戶部三十餘事，兵部十八事，工部十三事，詔悉厘正如舊制。
In the fifth year, in the fourth month, the Anhua prince Zhifan rebelled and posted a proclamation listing Jin's crimes. Jin finally became afraid, hid the proclamation, and appointed Grand Censor Yang Yiqing and eunuch Zhang Yong as commanders to suppress him. At first, among the Eight Tigers who were with Jin, when Jin monopolized the administration their requests were often not granted, and Yongcheng and Dayong and the others all resented him. He also wanted to drive Yong away, but Yong escaped through trickery. When Yong's army returned from the campaign, he wanted to use the opportunity to kill Jin; Yang Yiqing drew up the plan, and Yong's resolve was then set. Jin liked to gather sorcerers. There was one Yu Riming who falsely claimed that Jin's grandnephews, the Two Huns, were destined for great nobility. Eunuch Sun He of the Weapons Bureau repeatedly sent him armor and weapons, and the garrison supervisors Pan Wu and Cai Zhao of the two Guang regions also made bows and crossbows for him, all of which Jin stored in his home. When Yong's urgent memorial arrived, saying the prisoners would be presented on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, Jin had the date postponed. Yong feared there might be a change, so he entered ahead of schedule; after the prisoners were presented, the emperor set out wine to reward Yong, and Jin and the others all attended. That evening, after Jin withdrew, Yong produced Zhifan's proclamation and then memorialized seventeen crimes of Jin's unlawful conduct. The emperor had already been drinking, and with his head bowed he said: "Jin has betrayed me." Yong said: "This cannot be delayed." Yongcheng and the others also helped him. They then seized Jin and bound him in the vegetable depot, and sent officials and guards to seal up his private residences inside and outside the city. The next day, after the late court audience, the emperor brought out Yong's memorial and showed it to the Grand Secretariat, demoted Jin to fengyu, and banished him to Fengyang. The emperor personally inventoried his household and found a forged seal, five hundred palace passes, and forbidden items such as armor, bows, embroidered robes, and jade belts. In his usual fan there were also hidden two sharp daggers. The emperor at last flew into a great rage, saying: "The slave really has rebelled." He hastily sent him to prison. When the case was completed, an edict ordered him torn to pieces in the market, his head displayed on a pike, and the prison verdicts posted so the whole world could see the execution. His clan and the rebel faction were all executed. Zhang Cai died in prison, and his corpse was torn apart. Grand Secretariat ministers Jiao Fang, Liu Yu, and Cao Yuan, as well as ministers such as Bi Heng and Zhu En, more than sixty in all, were all demoted and banished. Afterward the court ministers memorialized on Jin's altered laws: twenty-four changes in the Ministry of Personnel, more than thirty in the Ministry of Revenue, eighteen in the Ministry of War, and thirteen in the Ministry of Works; an edict ordered all of them corrected back to the old regulations.
58
張永，保定新城人。 正德初，總神機營，與瑾為黨。 已而惡其所為，瑾亦覺其不附己也，言於帝，將黜之南京。 永知之，直趨帝前，訴瑾陷己。 帝召瑾與質，方爭辯，永輒奮拳毆瑾。 帝令谷大用等置酒為解，由是二人益不合。 及寘鐇反，命永及右都御史楊一清往討。 帝戎服送之東華門，賜關防、金瓜、鋼斧以行，寵遇甚盛。 瑾亦忌之，而帝方永，不能間也。 師出，寘鐇已擒，永遂率五百騎撫定余黨。 還次靈州，與一清言，欲奏瑾不法事。 一清曰：「彼在上左右，公言能必入乎？ 不如以計誅之。 」因為永畫策，永大喜，語詳一清傳。 是時，瑾兄都督同知景祥死，京師籍籍謂瑾將以八月十五日俟百官送葬，因作亂。 適永捷疏至，將以是日獻俘，瑾使緩其期，欲俟事成並擒永。 或以告永，永先期入獻俘，是夜遂奏誅瑾。
Zhang Yong. Zhang Yong was a man of Xincheng in Baoding. At the start of Zhengde he commanded the Divinely Mechanized Camp and was part of Jin's faction. Soon he came to dislike Jin's conduct, and Jin also sensed that he was no longer loyal; he spoke of him to the emperor and was about to dismiss him to Nanjing. Yong learned of it, went straight before the emperor, and complained that Jin was framing him. The emperor summoned Jin to confront him, and while they were arguing, Yong suddenly threw a punch and hit Jin. The emperor had Gu Dayong and the others set out wine to resolve it, and from that point the two were even less able to get along. When Zhifan rebelled, Yong and the Right Grand Censor Yang Yiqing were ordered to go and suppress him. The emperor sent them off in military dress at Donghua Gate and gave them passes, golden melons, and steel axes for the journey, showing them extraordinary favor. Jin also envied him, but the emperor favored Yong so much that he could not create discord. Before the army had gone far, Zhifan had already been captured, and Yong then led five hundred cavalry to pacify the remaining followers. When he reached Lingzhou on the return march, he spoke with Yang Yiqing and wanted to memorialize Jin's unlawful conduct. Yang Yiqing said, 'He is around the emperor. Are you sure your words can get in?' It would be better to kill him by a stratagem. Then he drew up a plan for Yong, who was greatly pleased. The details are in Yang Yiqing's biography. At that time, Jin's elder brother, the deputy regional commander Jing Xiang, died, and rumors spread in the capital that Jin would wait until the fifteenth day of the eighth month, when the officials came to escort the funeral, and then stage a revolt. Just then Yong's urgent memorial arrived, saying that he would present the captives on that day. Jin ordered the date postponed, hoping to wait until the matter succeeded and seize Yong as well. Someone informed Yong. Yong entered early to present the captives, and that night he memorialized the throne to have Jin executed.
59
於是英國公張懋、兵部尚書王敞等，奏永輯寧中外，兩建奇勛，遂封永兄富為泰安伯、弟容為安定伯。 涿州男子王豸嘗刺龍形及「人王」字於足，永以為妖人，擒之。 兵部尚書何鑒乞加永封，下廷臣議。 永欲身自封侯，引劉永誠、鄭和故事風廷臣，內閣以非制格之。 永意沮，乃辭免恩澤。 吏部尚書楊一清言宜聽永讓，以成其賢，事竟已。 久之，坐庫官盜庫銀事，閑住。 九年，北邊有警，命永督宣府、大同、延綏軍禦之，寇退乃還。
Thereupon Duke of Ying Zhang Mao, Minister of War Wang Chang, and others memorialized that Yong had pacified the court and the realm and had achieved two extraordinary merits, and so Yong's elder brother Fu was enfeoffed as Earl of Tai'an and his younger brother Rong as Earl of Anding. A man from Zhuozhou named Wang Zhi had once tattooed a dragon shape and the characters 'human king' on his foot. Yong took him for an evil sorcerer and seized him. Minister of War He Jian petitioned to add to Yong's title, and the matter was sent down for discussion by the ministers. Yong wanted to be enfeoffed personally as a marquis, citing the precedent of Liu Yongcheng and Zheng He to pressure the ministers, but the Grand Secretariat blocked it as contrary to the regulations. Yong's intention was discouraged, so he declined the bounty. Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing said that Yong should be allowed to yield, so as to complete his virtue, and the matter ended there. After a long while, he was placed on inactive duty because of the case of a treasury official stealing silver from the treasury. In the ninth year, there was trouble on the northern frontier. Yong was ordered to command the armies of Xuanfu, Datong, and Yansui against it, and he returned only after the enemy withdrew.
60
寧王宸濠反，帝南征，永率邊兵二千先行。 時王守仁已擒宸濠，檻車北上。 永以帝意遮守仁，欲縱宸濠於鄱陽湖，俟帝至與戰。 守仁不可，至杭州詣永。 永拒不見，守仁叱門者徑入，大呼曰：「我王守仁也，來與公議國家事，何拒我！ 」永為氣懾。 守仁因言江西荼毒已極，王師至，亂將不測。 永大悟，乃曰：「群小在側，永來，欲保護聖躬耳，非欲攘功也。 」因指江上檻車曰：「此宜歸我。 」守仁曰：「我何用此。 」即付永，而與永偕還江西。 時太監張忠等已從大江至南昌，方窮治逆黨，見永至，大沮。 永留數旬，促忠同歸，江西賴以安。 忠等屢讒守仁，亦賴永營解獲免。 武宗崩，永督九門防變。 世宗立，御史蕭淮奏谷大用、丘聚輩蠱惑先帝，黨惡為奸，並及永。 詔永閑住。 已而淮復劾永在江西不法事，再降永奉御，司香孝陵，然永在江西，實非有不法也。 嘉靖八年，大學士楊一清等言，永功大，不可泯，乃起永掌御用監，提督團營。 未幾卒。
When Prince Ning Chenhao rebelled, the emperor campaigned south, and Yong led 2,000 border troops ahead. At that time Wang Shouren had already captured Chenhao and was sending him north in a caged cart. Yong, relying on the emperor's intention, blocked Wang Shouren, wanting to release Chenhao at Poyang Lake and wait for the emperor to arrive and fight him. Shouren would not agree, and when he reached Hangzhou he went to see Yong. Yong refused to receive him. Shouren shouted at the gatekeeper and went straight in, calling out, 'I am Wang Shouren. I have come to discuss state affairs with you. Why refuse me!' Yong was cowed. Shouren then said that Jiangxi had already been ravaged to the limit, and when the imperial army arrived, the disorder would be beyond reckoning. Yong then realized it and said, 'With those petty men around me, I came only to protect the sacred person, not to seize the credit.' Then he pointed to the caged cart on the river and said, 'This should be returned to me.' Shouren said, 'What use would I have for this?' He immediately gave it to Yong, and the two returned together to Jiangxi. At that time, the eunuch Zhang Zhong and others had already come from the Yangzi River to Nanchang and were busy investigating the rebel party; when they saw Yong arrive, they were greatly frustrated. Yong stayed for several tens of days and urged Zhong to return with him, and Jiangxi relied on him to remain at peace. Zhong and the others repeatedly slandered Shouren, but they also relied on Yong's mediation to be spared. When the Wuzong died, Yong was put in charge of the Nine Gates to guard against disturbances. After the Shizong came to the throne, the censor Xiao Huai memorialized that Gu Dayong, Qiu Ju and their ilk had bewitched the former emperor, formed a gang of evil and done wrong, and included Yong as well. An edict ordered Yong to retire from office. Soon after, Huai again accused Yong of illegal acts in Jiangxi, and Yong was again demoted to palace service and assigned to the incense service at the Ming Tombs. But in fact Yong's conduct in Jiangxi had not been unlawful. In the eighth year of Jiajing, the Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and others said Yong's merit was great and could not be erased, so Yong was brought back to manage the Directorate of Imperial Household and supervise the Corps Camps. He died soon after.
61
谷大用
Gu Dayong
62
谷大用者，瑾掌司禮監時提督西廠，分遣官校遠出偵事。 江西南康民吳登顯等，五月五日為競渡，誣以擅造龍舟，籍其家，天下皆重足屏息。 建鷹房草場於安州，奪民田無數。 瑾誅，大用辭西廠。 未幾，帝復欲用之，大學士李東陽力諫乃止。 六年，劉六、劉七反，命大用總督軍務，偕伏羌伯毛銳、兵部侍郎陸完討之。 大用駐臨清，召邊將許泰、郤永、江彬、劉暉等入內地，聽調遣。 久之無功，會賊過鎮江狼山，遇颶風舟覆，陸完兵至殲之，遂封大用弟大亮為永清伯。 而先是平寘鐇時，其兄大寬已封高平伯矣，義子冒升賞者，不可勝紀。 世宗立，以迎立功賜金幣。 給事中閻閎極論之，尋降奉御，居南京。 已，召守康陵。 嘉靖十年籍其家。
Gu Dayong, when Jin was in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial, oversaw the Western Depot and sent officials and guards out to gather intelligence. When the people of Wu Dengxian and others in Nankang, Jiangxi, held dragon-boat races on the fifth day of the fifth month, he falsely accused them of making dragon boats without permission and confiscated their households, so that all under heaven stood on tiptoe and held their breath. He built an Eagle House and pasture grounds in Anzhou and seized countless people's fields. When Jin was executed, Dayong resigned from the Western Depot. Not long after, the emperor again wanted to use him, but the Grand Secretary Li Dongyang strongly remonstrated and stopped it. In the sixth year, Liu Liu and Liu Qi rebelled. Dayong was ordered to take overall command of the military affairs and, together with Earl of Fuqiang Mao Rui and Vice Minister of War Lu Wan, suppress them. Dayong was stationed at Linqing and summoned the frontier generals Xu Tai, Que Yong, Jiang Bin, Liu Hui, and others into the interior to await orders. After a long time no result was achieved. Then the rebels passed Mount Lang in Zhenjiang, where a gale overturned their boats. Lu Wan's troops arrived and annihilated them, and Dayong's younger brother Dayang was enfeoffed as Earl of Yongqing. Earlier, when Zhenzhi was pacified, his elder brother Dakuan had already been enfeoffed as Earl of Gaoping, and the number of adopted sons and men who advanced by merit cannot be counted. When the Shizong came to the throne, he was rewarded with gold and silk for having helped bring about the accession. The giving-attendance censor Yan Hong made a strong memorial against him, and soon after he was demoted to palace service and sent to live in Nanjing. After that, he was summoned to guard the Kangling Mausoleum. In the tenth year of Jiajing, his household was confiscated.
63
魏彬，當瑾時，總三千營。 瑾誅，代掌司禮監。 其年，敘寧夏功，封弟英鎮安伯，馬永成兄山亦封平涼伯。 世宗立，彬不自安，為英辭伯爵。 詔改都督同知，世襲錦衣指揮使。 給事中楊秉義、徐景嵩、吳嚴皆言彬附和逆瑾，結姻江彬，宜置極典。 帝宥不問。 已而御史復論之，始令閑住。
Wei Bin. Wei Bin, during Jin's time, was in charge of the Three Thousand Battalion. When Jin was executed, he took over the Directorate of Ceremonial. That year, in the account of the merits in Ningxia, his younger brother Ying was enfeoffed as Earl of Zhen'an, and Ma Yongcheng's elder brother Shan was also enfeoffed as Earl of Pingliang. After the Shizong came to the throne, Bin felt uneasy and resigned the earldom on Ying's behalf. An edict changed him to deputy regional commander and made him a hereditary Guard Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. The giving-attendance officials Yang Bingyi, Xu Jingsong, and Wu Yan all said Bin had followed and echoed the rebel Jin and had formed a marriage alliance with Jiang Bin, and should be punished with the severest law. The emperor pardoned him and did not inquire further. Soon after, the censors again memorialized against him, and he was at last ordered to retire from office.
64
張忠，霸州人。 正德時御馬太監，與司禮張雄、東廠張銳並侍豹房用事，時號三張，性皆凶悖。 忠利大盜張茂財，結為弟，引入豹房，侍帝蹴鞠。 而雄至怨其父不愛己致自宮，拒不見。 同儕勸之，乃垂簾杖其父，然後相抱泣，其無人理如此。 銳以捕妖言功，加祿至一百二十石。 每緝事，先令邏卒誘人為奸，乃捕之，得賄則釋，往往以危法中人。 三人並交通宸濠，受臧賢、錢寧等賄，以助成其叛。 寧王反，忠勸帝親征。 其遮王守仁捷，欲縱宸濠鄱陽，待帝自戰，皆忠之謀也。
Zhang Zhong. Zhang Zhong was a man of Bazhou. In the Zhengde reign, he was a eunuch of the imperial stables. Along with Zhang Xiong of the Directorate of Ceremonial and Zhang Rui of the Eastern Depot, he served in the Leopard Quarter and wielded power; the three were called the Three Zhangs, and all were ferocious and perverse in temperament. He took advantage of the great bandit Zhang Mao's wealth, made him a brother, brought him into the Leopard Quarter, and had him attend the emperor at polo. As for Xiong, he bitterly resented his father for not loving him and causing him to castrate himself, and he refused to see him. His companions urged him, so he lowered a curtain and beat his father with a staff, and only then did they embrace and weep; such was his lack of humanity. Rui gained merit by arresting sorcerous talk, and his salary was raised to 120 shi. Whenever he conducted investigations, he first ordered patrolmen to lure people into committing crimes, then arrested them; if they took bribes, he released them, often ensnaring people through harsh laws. The three all had dealings with Chenhao and accepted bribes from Zang Xian, Qian Ning, and others in order to help complete the rebellion. When the Prince of Ning rebelled, Zhong urged the emperor to lead the campaign in person. Their blocking of Wang Shouren's victory report and their plan to release Chenhao at Poyang and wait for the emperor to fight him were all Zhong's schemes.
65
是時，又有吳經者，尤親匿。 帝南征，經先至揚州。 嘗夜半燃炬通衢，遍入寡婦、處女家，掠以出，號哭震遠近，許以金贖，貧者多自經。 先是，又有劉允者，以正德十年奉敕往迎烏斯藏僧，所賫金寶以百餘萬計。 廷臣交章諫，不聽。 允至成都，治裝歲餘，費又數十萬，公私匱竭。 既至，為番人所襲。 允走免，將士死者數百人，盡亡其所賫。 及歸，武宗已崩，世宗用御史王鈞等言，張忠、吳經發孝陵衛充軍，張雄、張銳下都察院鞫治、允亦得罪。
At that time there was also a man named Wu Jing, who was especially close to him. When the emperor campaigned south, Jing arrived in Yangzhou first. At midnight he would light torches on the main streets, enter the homes of widows and maidens one by one, seize them and carry them off. Their crying shook near and far, and he promised they could ransom themselves with gold; many of the poor hanged themselves. Earlier there had also been a man named Liu Yun, who in the tenth year of Zhengde received an edict to go and welcome Tibetan monks, carrying gold and treasure worth more than a million. The ministers repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance, but he would not listen. When Yun reached Chengdu, it took more than a year to prepare, costing several hundred thousand more, and both public and private funds were exhausted. Once he arrived, he was attacked by the fan people. Yun escaped, but several hundred soldiers and officers died, and everything he had brought was lost. When he returned, the Wuzong had already died. The Shizong, taking the words of the censor Wang Jun and others, sent Zhang Zhong and Wu Jing to the Xiaoling Guard to serve as soldiers, sent Zhang Xiong and Zhang Rui to the Censorate for investigation and punishment, and Yun also incurred punishment.
66
世宗習見正德時宦侍之禍，即位後御近侍甚嚴，有罪撻之至死，或陳屍示戒。 張佐、鮑忠，麥福、黃錦輩，雖由興邸舊人掌司禮監，督東廠，然皆謹飭不敢大肆。 帝又盡撤天下鎮守內臣及典京營倉場者，終四十餘年不復設，故內臣之勢，惟嘉靖朝少殺云。
The Shizong had long witnessed the disasters caused by eunuch attendants in the Zhengde reign, and after his accession he kept a very strict hand on close attendants. Those who were guilty he beat to death, or displayed their bodies as a warning. Zhang Zuo, Bao Zhong, Mai Fu, Huang Jin, and the like, though they were old retainers of the Xing residence and held the Directorate of Ceremonial and supervised the Eastern Depot, were all cautious and disciplined and did not dare to run wild. The emperor also completely removed the inner eunuchs stationed throughout the empire and those in charge of the Beijing Camp granaries and stores; for more than forty years thereafter they were never restored. Thus the power of the inner eunuchs was diminished only slightly in the Jiajing reign.
